NgZ7N1W5ulQ.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 28: Eighth Night of Tahajjud
NgZ7N1W5ulQ.one_line: Between rakaat on the 28th night: those saved on the Day of Judgement look for their brothers, so the congregation pledges to take each other's hand.
NgZ7N1W5ulQ.summary: On the twenty-eighth night of Ramadan 2026 the single reminder between rakaat builds to a shared act the congregation is meant to remember. Starting from a verse recited that night in Az-Zumar, that Allah will save the God-conscious and grant them success, he turns to salvation on the Day of Judgement: after crossing the bridge over Hell there comes a moment on the far side when a person knows he is saved. That is the deep reason it is recommended to get to know as many believers as possible: once across, you look around for the people you knew and ask where they are. At the arched bridge before Paradise and in the places where Allah permits intercession, believers plead for their brothers and sisters, and that, he says, is what brotherhood means. He then asks everyone to take the hands of the people on their right and left and make a covenant that whoever among them is saved will take his brother's or sister's hand on that Day, reminding them that Allah commands fulfilling covenants, and closes asking Allah to save them all from the Fire.

uBpazmjT1kc.speaker_note: a teacher who refers to his own Arabic class runs a group workshop on similar verses and hands over to a student speaker at the end; not the sheikh
uBpazmjT1kc.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 27: Workshop on Similar Verses (Adh-Dhariyat and Al-Ma'arij)
uBpazmjT1kc.one_line: A group exercise comparing two similar passages: the muhsinin of Adh-Dhariyat who go beyond, and the musallin of Al-Ma'arij who keep the minimum.
uBpazmjT1kc.summary: The speaker shows that clusters of verses that sound alike, which reciters often confuse, are never random. He gives four tools for comparing them: context before and after, keywords, subtle differences in wording and word order, and the occasion of revelation, noting that Arabic fronts what matters most, as in 'You alone we worship'. Groups then compare Adh-Dhariyat 51:15-19 with Al-Ma'arij 70:19-35. In Adh-Dhariyat the muhsinin, people who go the extra mile, sleep little at night, seek forgiveness before dawn, and give the asker and the deprived an unspecified right in their wealth. In Al-Ma'arij the anxious, grasping human is excepted only if he is one of the musallin, a noun describing people whose identity is prayer: they keep it constantly, recognise a known right of others in their wealth, believe in the Day of Judgment, are deeply concerned about their Lord's punishment, guard their chastity, keep trusts and covenants, uphold testimony and protect their prayers. He concludes that Al-Ma'arij sets the floor no believer may fall below, while Adh-Dhariyat describes a higher rank of voluntary excellence, and urges reading the Quran slowly with attention to such differences.

outline.heading: Similar clusters at the end of the Quran
outline.gist: Some passages share wording and even verse length but are not identical; the exercise is to find out why.

outline.heading: Interlude
Not random: look at the context
outline.gist: Reciters confuse such passages; first assume a reason and read what comes before and after.

outline.heading: Keywords and subtle differences
outline.gist: Each cluster has a keyword that Allah builds on, and the wording differs in small, meaningful ways.

outline.heading: The keyword of each passage
outline.gist: One passage builds on the muhsinin, the other on the human being and his description.

outline.heading: Occasion of revelation and word order
outline.gist: Arabic fronts what is most important, as in 'You alone we worship' rather than 'we worship You'.

outline.heading: Interlude
They slept little of the night
outline.gist: Fronting 'little' emphasizes how little they slept, spending the night in prayer and dua.

outline.heading: Seeking forgiveness before dawn
outline.gist: The same fronting highlights that the pre-dawn hours are given to istighfar.

outline.heading: A right, but not a known right
outline.gist: Adh-Dhariyat says 'a right' for the asker and the deprived, while Al-Ma'arij says 'a known right': voluntary giving versus the fixed obligation.

outline.heading: Muhsinin: those who go the extra mile
outline.gist: Ihsan always describes doing more than required, such as staying up at night and giving without counting.

outline.heading: Read slowly and look before and after
outline.gist: Reciting is not enough; contemplate the verse, the page before and the page after.

outline.heading: The anxious human being
outline.gist: The insan is never praised in the Quran: impatient, despairing in hardship and withholding in ease.

outline.heading: Except the musallin: prayer as identity
outline.gist: The noun musallin, rather than 'those who pray', describes people so constant in prayer that it defines them.

outline.heading: Constant in their prayer
outline.gist: Their day is scheduled around the prayer times.

outline.heading: A known right in their wealth
outline.gist: Part of every income belongs to someone else; the sunnah fixes it at two and a half percent for the asker and the deprived.

outline.heading: Interlude
From outward practice to inner belief
outline.gist: These verses set the bare minimum; after the physical practices come what they believe.

outline.heading: Believing in the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: Belief in accountability is what keeps a person from despair in hardship and stinginess in ease.

outline.heading: Concerned about their Lord's punishment
outline.gist: Mushfiqun means ongoing concern, which differs from simple fear.

outline.heading: Guarding chastity
outline.gist: No relationships outside what Islam permits; those who seek beyond it are transgressors who cross the line.

outline.heading: Keeping trusts and covenants
outline.gist: The amanah the heavens and mountains declined includes every covenant with Allah and every trust between people.

outline.heading: None of these may be broken
outline.gist: Unlike night prayer, these qualities are not optional; truthful testimony is among them.

outline.heading: Beginning and ending with prayer
outline.gist: The passage opens with constancy in prayer and closes with guarding it, and its people are honoured in gardens.

outline.heading: Which group ranks higher?
outline.gist: The muhsinin go above and beyond and rank higher; the musallin describe the floor no believer can go below.

outline.heading: Another similar cluster and repeated stories
outline.gist: The opening of Al-Mu'minun sounds similar again; repeated stories such as Nuh and Adam are each worded differently for a reason.

outline.heading: Interlude
Question: is the fuller description lower?
outline.gist: A questioner notes Al-Ma'arij lists more qualities; he answers that its items are obligatory, while the muhsinin give without limit.

outline.heading: Outro

My Lord hath made it true, and He hath shown me kindness, since He took me out of the prison and hath brought you from the desert after Satan had made strife between me and my brethren. Lo! my Lord is tender unto whom He will. He is the Knower, the Wise

66:8.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ تُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوۡبَةࣰ نَّصُوحًا عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمۡ أَن يُكَفِّرَ عَنكُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمۡ وَيُدۡخِلَكُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ يَوۡمَ لَا يُخۡزِي ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّبِيَّ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥۖ نُورُهُمۡ يَسۡعَىٰ بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَبِأَيۡمَٰنِهِمۡ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَتۡمِمۡ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
66:8.en: O ye who believe! Turn unto Allah in sincere repentance! It may be that your Lord will remit from you your evil deeds and bring you into Gardens underneath which rivers flow, on the day when Allah will not abase the Prophet and those who believe with him. Their light will run before them and on their right hands; they will say: Our Lord! Perfect our light for us, and forgive us! Lo! Thou art Able to do all things

42:25.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَقۡبَلُ ٱلتَّوۡبَةَ عَنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَعۡفُواْ عَنِ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا تَفۡعَلُونَ
42:25.en: And He it is Who accepteth repentance from His bondmen, and pardoneth the evil deeds, and knoweth what ye do

25:68.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَدۡعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ وَلَا يَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا يَزۡنُونَۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٰلِكَ يَلۡقَ أَثَامࣰ ا
25:68.en: And those who cry not unto any other god along with Allah, nor take the life which Allah hath forbidden save in (course of) justice, nor commit adultery - and whoso doeth this shall pay the penalty

25:69.ar: يُضَٰعَفۡ لَهُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَيَخۡلُدۡ فِيهِۦ مُهَانًا
25:69.en: The doom will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein disdained for ever

25:70.ar: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلࣰ ا صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ حَسَنَٰتࣲۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
25:70.en: Save him who repenteth and believeth and doth righteous work; as for such, Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

1hBPaO-AKfI.speaker: guest
1hBPaO-AKfI.speaker_note: a different speaker delivers a structured, student-style talk in mixed Arabic and English; the title names no speaker and the delivery is not the sheikh's
1hBPaO-AKfI.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 27: Tawbah and Forgiveness
1hBPaO-AKfI.one_line: Using the last nights to seek forgiveness: Allah's names of forgiveness, forgiving others like Abu Bakr and Yusuf, and the conditions of sincere tawbah.
1hBPaO-AKfI.summary: The speaker starts from Ramadan being a counted number of days that pass quickly, like life itself, and the story of two companions where the one who lived a year longer, fasting and praying more, entered paradise first. The last nights are like a treasure room open for thirty minutes, and forgiveness is its greatest treasure, since the one who reaches Ramadan unforgiven is warned and Laylat al-Qadr can equal a lifetime. He distinguishes istighfar from tawbah: major or repeated sins need regret and a plan to change. He explains Al-Ghafur and Al-Ghaffar, from a root meaning to cover, and Allah's concealment of our sins; every human errs, and the best are those who keep returning, as a child gets back on the bike. The Quran tells us to walk for provision but to race toward forgiveness and flee to Allah. Forgiving others is a path to being forgiven, as with Abu Bakr and Mistah and Yusuf, who forgave his brothers without reminding them. Tawbah is returning to the path like a rerouting map, and its conditions are stopping the sin, regret, resolving not to return, and repairing harm, after which Allah turns bad deeds into good.

outline.heading: Opening
A counted number of days
outline.gist: Ramadan passes as quickly as life does; with three nights left, ask whether you used the time well.

outline.heading: The companion who lived one more year
outline.gist: Of two men who accepted Islam together, the one who outlived the martyr by a year entered paradise first, because of the extra Ramadan and prayers.

outline.heading: A treasure room open for thirty minutes
outline.gist: Would you spend limited access to a room of treasure scrolling Instagram, or seek the most valuable thing in it?

outline.heading: Forgiveness, the greatest treasure
outline.gist: The Prophet said ameen on the minbar to Jibril's dua against one who reaches Ramadan and is not forgiven.

outline.heading: Laylat al-Qadr: one moment worth a lifetime
outline.gist: A single act of high-quality worship can earn the reward of a thousand months; this may be our last chance.

outline.heading: Istighfar versus tawbah
outline.gist: For major or repeated sins asking forgiveness is not enough; one must regret the sin and plan to rectify it.

outline.heading: Maghfirah means covering
outline.gist: The root of Allah's names of forgiveness means to cover; His concealment of our sins is a mercy, or we could not face one another.

outline.heading: Al-Ghafur and Al-Ghaffar
outline.gist: Al-Ghafur forgives every kind of sin, great and small; Al-Ghaffar, in an intensive form, keeps forgiving time after time.

outline.heading: Every human errs; get back on the bike
outline.gist: The best sinners are those who repent; like a child who falls off a bike, we keep returning to Allah, who forgives sins that reach the sky.

outline.heading: Everything forgiven except shirk
outline.gist: Allah forgives all sins below associating partners with Him for whom He wills.

outline.heading: Walk for provision, race for forgiveness
outline.gist: The Quran says to walk the earth for provision but to hasten and compete for forgiveness.

outline.heading: Remember Allah and flee to Him
outline.gist: Those who wrong themselves remember Allah and seek forgiveness; the believer flees back to Him.

outline.heading: Forgive to be forgiven: Abu Bakr and Mistah
outline.gist: After the slander against Aisha, Abu Bakr swore to stop supporting Mistah, and was told: do you not love that Allah forgive you?

outline.heading: Yusuf forgives his brothers
outline.gist: Thrown in a well, enslaved and imprisoned, Yusuf told his brothers there is no blame today and later mentioned only the prison, blaming Shaytan for the rift.

outline.heading: Forgiveness without reminding
outline.gist: Real forgiveness does not keep count, humiliate or remind the person; ask who in your life you can forgive.

outline.heading: Tawbah means returning to the route
outline.gist: Sincere repentance is like a map app rerouting you to the original path after a wrong turn; At-Tawwab keeps accepting the return.

outline.heading: A clean slate
outline.gist: Allah accepts repentance from His servants and pardons their bad deeds.

outline.heading: Come walking and He comes running
outline.gist: In a hadith qudsi, whoever meets Allah with an earth-full of sins, without shirk, is met with as much forgiveness.

outline.heading: First condition: stop the sin
outline.gist: You cannot claim to return to Allah while still committing the sin.

outline.heading: Second condition: genuine regret
outline.gist: Without believing the act is wrong, as with someone who does not think smoking is haram, behaviour never changes.

outline.heading: Third condition: a plan not to return
outline.gist: Identify what pulls you back, such as friends or environment, and plan how to leave it.

outline.heading: Fourth condition: repair the harm
outline.gist: Those who repent, believe and do righteous deeds have their bad deeds replaced with good ones.

outline.heading: Transformed in the last nights
outline.gist: He asks that we leave Ramadan forgiven, transformed and connected to the Quran.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Tawbah is returning to the path; for major or repeated sins it requires stopping, regret, a plan and repairing harm.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Al-Ghafur, Al-Ghaffar and At-Tawwab describe a Lord who covers sins and keeps forgiving.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Forgiving others, without reminding or humiliating them, is a way to earn Allah's forgiveness.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: The last nights are a limited treasure room whose greatest prize is forgiveness.

themes.label: Time, opportunity and seizing the moment
themes.note: One extra year of fasting and prayer raised a companion above a martyr; time slips by like Ramadan.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Yusuf's forgiveness of his brothers is the model of forgiving without reproach.

quran.point: Fasting is for a counted number of days.
Laylat al-Qadr is better than a thousand months.
By time, mankind is in loss.
Allah does not forgive shirk but forgives anything less for whom He wills.
After prayer disperse in the land and seek Allah's bounty.
Walk through the earth and eat of His provision: walking for rizq.
Hasten to forgiveness from your Lord.
Race toward forgiveness from your Lord.
Those who commit an indecency or wrong themselves remember Allah and seek forgiveness.
So flee to Allah.
Let them pardon and overlook; do you not love that Allah forgive you?
No blame on you today.
Yusuf mentions being freed from prison and blames Shaytan for the rift, not his brothers.
Turn to Allah in sincere repentance.
He accepts repentance from His servants and pardons bad deeds.
Except whoever repents, believes and does righteous deeds: Allah replaces their bad deeds with good.

hadith.gist: Talhah dreamt that of two companions, the one who died a year after the martyr entered paradise first; the Prophet explained he had fasted another Ramadan and prayed so many more prayers.
The Prophet said ameen on the minbar when Jibril prayed against the one who reaches Ramadan and is not forgiven.
Allah looked at the people of Badr and said do as you wish, for I have forgiven you.
Every child of Adam errs, and the best of those who err are those who repent.
O son of Adam, as long as you call on Me and hope in Me I will forgive you, even if your sins reach the clouds of the sky.
Whoever comes to Allah walking, He comes to him running; whoever meets Him with an earth-full of sins without shirk, He meets with as much forgiveness.

maxims: Walk for provision, race for forgiveness
Forgiveness that comes with counting is not forgiveness

stories.who: Two companions, one martyred and one who lived a year longer
stories.point: An extra Ramadan of fasting and prayer can outweigh martyrdom; value the time left.

stories.who: Abu Bakr and Mistah after the slander of Aisha
stories.point: Forgiving those who wronged you is how you seek Allah's forgiveness.

stories.who: Yusuf and his brothers
stories.point: True forgiveness never reminds or humiliates the one forgiven.

takeaways: Treat the remaining nights as limited access to a treasure and seek forgiveness above all.
For repeated or major sins, stop, regret, plan to avoid the triggers, and repair any harm done.
Forgive someone who wronged you, and do not remind them of it afterwards.
Keep returning to Allah after every fall instead of giving up.

51:1.en: By those that winnow with a winnowing

51:2.en: And those that bear the burden (of the rain)

51:3.en: And those that glide with ease (upon the sea)

51:4.en: And those who distribute (blessings) by command

51:5.en: Lo! that wherewith ye are threatened is indeed true

51:6.en: And lo! the judgment will indeed befall

51:7.en: By the heaven full of paths

51:8.en: Lo! ye, forsooth, are of various opinion (concerning the truth)

51:9.en: He is made to turn away from it who is (himself) averse

51:11.en: Who are careless in an abyss

51:12.en: They ask: When is the Day of Judgment

51:13.en: (It is) the day when they will be tormented at the Fire

51:14.ar: ذُوقُواْ فِتۡنَتَكُمۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَسۡتَعۡجِلُونَ
51:14.en: (And it will be said unto them): Taste your torment (which ye inflicted). This is what ye sought to hasten

51:15.en: Lo! those who keep from evil will dwell amid gardens and watersprings

51:16.ar: ءَاخِذِينَ مَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمۡ رَبُّهُمۡۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَبۡلَ ذَٰلِكَ مُحۡسِنِينَ
51:16.en: Taking that which their Lord giveth them; for lo! aforetime they were doers of good

51:17.ar: كَانُواْ قَلِيلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ مَا يَهۡجَعُونَ
51:17.en: They used to sleep but little of the night

51:18.en: And ere the dawning of each day would seek forgiveness

51:19.en: And in their wealth the beggar and the outcast had due share

51:20.en: And in the earth are portents for those whose faith is sure

51:21.en: And (also) in yourselves. Can ye then not see

51:22.en: And in the heaven is your providence and that which ye are promised

51:23.ar: فَوَرَبِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِنَّهُۥ لَحَقࣱّ مِّثۡلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمۡ تَنطِقُونَ
51:23.en: And by the Lord of the heavens and the earth, it is the truth, even as (it is true) that ye speak

51:24.ar: هَلۡ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيۡفِ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ ٱلۡمُكۡرَمِينَ
51:24.en: Hath the story of Abraham's honoured guests reached thee (O Muhammad)

51:25.ar: إِذۡ دَخَلُواْ عَلَيۡهِ فَقَالُواْ سَلَٰمࣰ اۖ قَالَ سَلَٰمࣱ قَوۡمࣱ مُّنكَرُونَ
51:25.en: When they came in unto him and said: Peace! he answered, Peace! (and thought): Folk unknown (to me)

51:26.ar: فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجۡلࣲ سَمِينࣲ‏
51:26.en: Then he went apart unto his housefolk so that they brought a fatted calf

51:27.en: And he set it before them, saying: Will ye not eat

51:28.ar: فَأَوۡجَسَ مِنۡهُمۡ خِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُواْ لَا تَخَفۡۖ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ عَلِيمࣲ‏
51:28.en: Then he conceived a fear of them. They said: Fear not! and gave him tidings of (the birth of) a wise son

51:29.ar: فَأَقۡبَلَتِ ٱمۡرَأَتُهُۥ فِي صَرَّةࣲ فَصَكَّتۡ وَجۡهَهَا وَقَالَتۡ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمࣱ‏
51:29.en: Then his wife came forward, making moan, and smote her face, and cried: A barren old woman

51:30.ar: قَالُواْ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
51:30.en: They said: Even so saith thy Lord. Lo! He is the Wise, the Knower

51:31.en: (Abraham) said: And (afterward) what is your errand, O ye sent (from Allah)

51:32.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّآ أُرۡسِلۡنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمࣲ مُّجۡرِمِينَ
51:32.en: They said: Lo! we are sent unto a guilty folk

51:33.en: That we may send upon them stones of clay

51:34.en: Marked by thy Lord for (the destruction of) the wanton

51:35.ar: فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا مَن كَانَ فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
51:35.en: Then we brought forth such believers as were there

51:36.ar: فَمَا وَجَدۡنَا فِيهَا غَيۡرَ بَيۡتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
51:36.en: But We found there but one house of those surrendered (to Allah)

51:37.ar: وَتَرَكۡنَا فِيهَآ ءَايَةࣰ لِّلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ ٱلۡأَلِيمَ
51:37.en: And We left behind therein a portent for those who fear a painful doom

51:38.ar: وَفِي مُوسَىٰٓ إِذۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ بِسُلۡطَٰنࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
51:38.en: And in Moses (too, there is a portent) when We sent him unto Pharaoh with clear warrant

51:39.ar: فَتَوَلَّىٰ بِرُكۡنِهِۦ وَقَالَ سَٰحِرٌ أَوۡ مَجۡنُونࣱ‏
51:39.en: But he withdrew (confiding) in his might, and said: A wizard or a madman

51:40.ar: فَأَخَذۡنَٰهُ وَجُنُودَهُۥ فَنَبَذۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّ وَهُوَ مُلِيمࣱ‏
51:40.en: So We seized him and his hosts and flung them in the sea, for he was reprobate

51:41.ar: وَفِي عَادٍ إِذۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلرِّيحَ ٱلۡعَقِيمَ
51:41.en: And in (the tribe of) A'ad (there is a portent) when we sent the fatal wind against them

51:42.ar: مَا تَذَرُ مِن شَيۡءٍ أَتَتۡ عَلَيۡهِ إِلَّا جَعَلَتۡهُ كَٱلرَّمِيمِ
51:42.en: It spared naught that it reached, but made it (all) as dust

51:43.ar: وَفِي ثَمُودَ إِذۡ قِيلَ لَهُمۡ تَمَتَّعُواْ حَتَّىٰ حِينࣲ‏
51:43.en: And in (the tribe of) Thamud (there is a portent) when it was told them: Take your ease awhile

51:44.ar: فَعَتَوۡاْ عَنۡ أَمۡرِ رَبِّهِمۡ فَأَخَذَتۡهُمُ ٱلصَّٰعِقَةُ وَهُمۡ يَنظُرُونَ
51:44.en: But they rebelled against their Lord's decree, and so the thunderbolt overtook them even while they gazed

51:45.ar: فَمَا ٱسۡتَطَٰعُواْ مِن قِيَامࣲ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُنتَصِرِينَ
51:45.en: And they were unable to rise up, nor could they help themselves

51:46.ar: وَقَوۡمَ نُوحࣲ مِّن قَبۡلُۖ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَوۡمࣰ ا فَٰسِقِينَ
51:46.en: And the folk of Noah aforetime. Lo! they were licentious folk

51:47.en: We have built the heaven with might, and We it is Who make the vast extent (thereof)

51:48.en: And the earth have We laid out, how gracious is the Spreader (thereof)

51:49.ar: وَمِن كُلِّ شَيۡءٍ خَلَقۡنَا زَوۡجَيۡنِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ
51:49.en: And all things We have created by pairs, that haply ye may reflect

51:50.ar: فَفِرُّوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ إِنِّي لَكُم مِّنۡهُ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
51:50.en: Therefor flee unto Allah; lo! I am a plain warner unto you from him

51:51.ar: وَلَا تَجۡعَلُواْ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَۖ إِنِّي لَكُم مِّنۡهُ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
51:51.en: And set not any other god along with Allah; lo! I am a plain warner unto you from Him

51:52.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ مَآ أَتَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا قَالُواْ سَاحِرٌ أَوۡ مَجۡنُونٌ
51:52.en: Even so there came no messenger unto those before them but they said: A wizard or a madman

51:53.ar: أَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِهِۦۚ بَلۡ هُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ طَاغُونَ
51:53.en: Have they handed down (the saying) as an heirloom one unto another? Nay, but they are froward folk

51:54.en: So withdraw from them (O Muhammad), for thou art in no wise blameworthy

51:55.en: And warn, for warning profiteth believers

51:56.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡتُ ٱلۡجِنَّ وَٱلۡإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُونِ
51:56.en: I created the jinn and humankind only that they might worship Me

51:57.ar: مَآ أُرِيدُ مِنۡهُم مِّن رِّزۡقࣲ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَن يُطۡعِمُونِ
51:57.en: I seek no livelihood from them, nor do I ask that they should feed Me

51:58.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلرَّزَّاقُ ذُو ٱلۡقُوَّةِ ٱلۡمَتِينُ
51:58.en: Lo! Allah! He it is that giveth livelihood, the Lord of unbreakable might

51:59.ar: فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ ذَنُوبࣰ ا مِّثۡلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصۡحَٰبِهِمۡ فَلَا يَسۡتَعۡجِلُونِ
51:59.en: And lo! for those who (now) do wrong there is an evil day like unto the evil day (which came for) their likes (of old); so let them not ask Me to hasten on (that day)

51:60.ar: فَوَيۡلࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن يَوۡمِهِمُ ٱلَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ
51:60.en: And woe unto those who disbelieve, from (that) their day which they are promised

52:7.en: Lo! the doom of thy Lord will surely come to pass

52:8.en: There is none that can ward it off

52:9.en: On the day when the heaven will heave with (awful) heaving

52:10.en: And the mountains move away with (awful) movement

52:11.en: Then woe that day unto the deniers

52:12.en: Who play in talk of grave matters

52:13.ar: يَوۡمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَىٰ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا
52:13.en: The day when they are thrust with a (disdainful) thrust, into the fire of hell

52:14.ar: هَٰذِهِ ٱلنَّارُ ٱلَّتِي كُنتُم بِهَا تُكَذِّبُونَ
52:14.en: (And it is said unto them): This is the Fire which ye were wont to deny

52:15.ar: أَفَسِحۡرٌ هَٰذَآ أَمۡ أَنتُمۡ لَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
52:15.en: Is this magic, or do ye not see

52:16.ar: ٱصۡلَوۡهَا فَٱصۡبِرُوٓاْ أَوۡ لَا تَصۡبِرُواْ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡۖ إِنَّمَا تُجۡزَوۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
52:16.en: Endure the heat thereof, and whether ye are patient of it or impatient of it is all one for you. Ye are only being paid for what ye used to do

52:17.en: Lo! those who kept their duty dwell in gardens and delight

52:18.ar: فَٰكِهِينَ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمۡ رَبُّهُمۡ وَوَقَىٰهُمۡ رَبُّهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
52:18.en: Happy because of what their Lord hath given them, and (because) their Lord hath warded off from them the torment of hell-fire

52:19.ar: كُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ هَنِيٓـَٔۢا بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
52:19.en: (And it is said unto them): Eat and drink in health (as a reward) for what ye used to do

52:20.ar: مُتَّكِـِٔينَ عَلَىٰ سُرُرࣲ مَّصۡفُوفَةࣲۖ وَزَوَّجۡنَٰهُم بِحُورٍ عِينࣲ‏
52:20.en: Reclining on ranged couches. And we wed them unto fair ones with wide, lovely eyes

52:21.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَٱتَّبَعَتۡهُمۡ ذُرِّيَّتُهُم بِإِيمَٰنٍ أَلۡحَقۡنَا بِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمۡ وَمَآ أَلَتۡنَٰهُم مِّنۡ عَمَلِهِم مِّن شَيۡءࣲۚ كُلُّ ٱمۡرِيِٕۭ بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهِينࣱ‏
52:21.en: And they who believe and whose seed follow them in faith, We cause their seed to join them (there), and We deprive them of nought of their (life's) work. Every man is a pledge for that which he hath earned

52:22.en: And We provide them with fruit and meat such as they desire

52:23.ar: يَتَنَٰزَعُونَ فِيهَا كَأۡسࣰ ا لَّا لَغۡوࣱ فِيهَا وَلَا تَأۡثِيمࣱ‏
52:23.en: There they pass from hand to hand a cup wherein is neither vanity nor cause of sin

52:24.ar: ۞وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ غِلۡمَانࣱ لَّهُمۡ كَأَنَّهُمۡ لُؤۡلُؤࣱ مَّكۡنُونࣱ‏
52:24.en: And there go round, waiting on them menservants of their own, as they were hidden pearls

52:25.en: And some of them draw near unto others, questioning

52:26.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا كُنَّا قَبۡلُ فِيٓ أَهۡلِنَا مُشۡفِقِينَ
52:26.en: Saying: Lo! of old, when we were with our families, we were ever anxious

52:27.ar: فَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا وَوَقَىٰنَا عَذَابَ ٱلسَّمُومِ
52:27.en: But Allah hath been gracious unto us and hath preserved us from the torment of the breath of Fire

52:28.ar: إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبۡلُ نَدۡعُوهُۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡبَرُّ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
52:28.en: Lo! we used to pray unto Him of old. Lo! He is the Benign, the Merciful

52:29.ar: فَذَكِّرۡ فَمَآ أَنتَ بِنِعۡمَتِ رَبِّكَ بِكَاهِنࣲ وَلَا مَجۡنُونٍ
52:29.en: Therefor warn (men, O Muhammad). By the grace of Allah thou art neither soothsayer nor madman

52:30.ar: أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ شَاعِرࣱ نَّتَرَبَّصُ بِهِۦ رَيۡبَ ٱلۡمَنُونِ
52:30.en: Or say they: (he is) a poet, (one) for whom we may expect the accident of time

52:31.ar: قُلۡ تَرَبَّصُواْ فَإِنِّي مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡمُتَرَبِّصِينَ
52:31.en: Say (unto them): Except (your fill)! Lo! I am with you among the expectant

52:32.ar: أَمۡ تَأۡمُرُهُمۡ أَحۡلَٰمُهُم بِهَٰذَآۚ أَمۡ هُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ طَاغُونَ
52:32.en: Do their minds command them to do this, or are they an outrageous folk

52:33.ar: أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ تَقَوَّلَهُۥۚ بَل لَّا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
52:33.en: Or say they: He hath invented it? Nay, but they will not believe

52:34.ar: فَلۡيَأۡتُواْ بِحَدِيثࣲ مِّثۡلِهِۦٓ إِن كَانُواْ صَٰدِقِينَ
52:34.en: Then let them produce speech the like thereof, if they are truthful

52:35.ar: أَمۡ خُلِقُواْ مِنۡ غَيۡرِ شَيۡءٍ أَمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰلِقُونَ
52:35.en: Or were they created out of naught? Or are they the creators

52:36.ar: أَمۡ خَلَقُواْ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَۚ بَل لَّا يُوقِنُونَ
52:36.en: Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Nay, but they are sure of nothing

52:37.ar: أَمۡ عِندَهُمۡ خَزَآئِنُ رَبِّكَ أَمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡمُصَۜيۡطِرُونَ
52:37.en: Or do they own the treasures of thy Lord? Or have they been given charge (thereof)

52:38.ar: أَمۡ لَهُمۡ سُلَّمࣱ يَسۡتَمِعُونَ فِيهِۖ فَلۡيَأۡتِ مُسۡتَمِعُهُم بِسُلۡطَٰنࣲ مُّبِينٍ
52:38.en: Or have they any stairway (unto heaven) by means of which they overhear (decrees). Then let their listener produce some warrant manifest

52:39.en: Or hath He daughters whereas ye have sons

52:40.ar: أَمۡ تَسۡـَٔلُهُمۡ أَجۡرࣰ ا فَهُم مِّن مَّغۡرَمࣲ مُّثۡقَلُونَ
52:40.en: Or askest thou (Muhammad) a fee from them so that they are plunged in debt

52:41.en: Or possess they the Unseen so that they can write (it) down

52:42.ar: أَمۡ يُرِيدُونَ كَيۡدࣰ اۖ فَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ هُمُ ٱلۡمَكِيدُونَ
52:42.en: Or seek they to ensnare (the messenger)? But those who disbelieve, they are the ensnared

52:43.ar: أَمۡ لَهُمۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِۚ سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
52:43.en: Or have they any god beside Allah? Glorified be Allah from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)

52:44.ar: وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ كِسۡفࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ سَاقِطࣰ ا يَقُولُواْ سَحَابࣱ مَّرۡكُومࣱ‏
52:44.en: And if they were to see a fragment of the heaven falling, they would say: A heap of clouds

52:45.ar: فَذَرۡهُمۡ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُواْ يَوۡمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِي فِيهِ يُصۡعَقُونَ
52:45.en: Then let them be (O Muhammad), till they meet their day, in which they will be thunder-stricken

52:46.ar: يَوۡمَ لَا يُغۡنِي عَنۡهُمۡ كَيۡدُهُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا هُمۡ يُنصَرُونَ
52:46.en: A day in which their guile will naught avail them, nor will they be helped

52:47.ar: وَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ عَذَابࣰ ا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
52:47.en: And verily, for those who do wrong, there is a punishment beyond that. But most of them know not

52:48.ar: وَٱصۡبِرۡ لِحُكۡمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعۡيُنِنَاۖ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ
52:48.en: So wait patiently (O Muhammad) for thy Lord's decree, for surely thou art in Our sight; and hymn the praise of thy Lord when thou uprisest

52:49.en: And in the night-time also hymn His praise, and at the setting of the stars

53:1.en: By the Star when it setteth

53:2.en: Your comrade erreth not, nor is deceived

53:3.en: Nor doth he speak of (his own) desire

53:4.en: It is naught save an inspiration that is inspired

53:5.en: Which one of mighty powers hath taught him

53:6.en: One vigorous; and he grew clear to view

53:7.en: When he was on the uppermost horizon

53:8.en: Then he drew nigh and came down

53:9.en: Till he was (distant) two bows' length or even nearer

53:10.en: And He revealed unto His slave that which He revealed

53:11.en: The heart lied not (in seeing) what it saw

53:12.en: Will ye then dispute with him concerning what he seeth

53:13.en: And verily he saw him yet another time

53:14.en: By the lote-tree of the utmost boundary

53:15.en: Nigh unto which is the Garden of Abode

53:16.en: When that which shroudeth did enshroud the lote-tree

53:17.en: The eye turned not aside nor yet was overbold

53:18.ar: لَقَدۡ رَأَىٰ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّهِ ٱلۡكُبۡرَىٰٓ
53:18.en: Verily he saw one of the greater revelations of his Lord

53:19.en: Have ye thought upon Al-Lat and Al-'Uzza

53:20.en: And Manat, the third, the other

53:21.en: Are yours the males and His the females

53:22.en: That indeed were an unfair division

53:23.ar: إِنۡ هِيَ إِلَّآ أَسۡمَآءࣱ سَمَّيۡتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمۡ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلۡطَٰنٍۚ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهۡوَى ٱلۡأَنفُسُۖ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَهُم مِّن رَّبِّهِمُ ٱلۡهُدَىٰٓ
53:23.en: They are but names which ye have named, ye and your fathers, for which Allah hath revealed no warrant. They follow but a guess and that which (they) themselves desire. And now the guidance from their Lord hath come unto them

53:24.en: Or shall man have what he coveteth

53:25.en: But unto Allah belongeth the after (life), and the former

53:26.ar: ۞وَكَم مِّن مَّلَكࣲ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ لَا تُغۡنِي شَفَٰعَتُهُمۡ شَيۡـًٔا إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ أَن يَأۡذَنَ ٱللَّهُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَرۡضَىٰٓ
53:26.en: And how many angels are in the heavens whose intercession availeth naught save after Allah giveth leave to whom He chooseth and accepteth

53:27.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ لَيُسَمُّونَ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ تَسۡمِيَةَ ٱلۡأُنثَىٰ
53:27.en: Lo! it is those who disbelieve in the Hereafter who name the angels with the names of females

53:28.ar: وَمَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنۡ عِلۡمٍۖ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّۖ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لَا يُغۡنِي مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا
53:28.en: And they have no knowledge thereof. They follow but a guess, and lo! a guess can never take the place of the truth

53:29.ar: فَأَعۡرِضۡ عَن مَّن تَوَلَّىٰ عَن ذِكۡرِنَا وَلَمۡ يُرِدۡ إِلَّا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا
53:29.en: Then withdraw (O Muhammad) from him who fleeth from Our remembrance and desireth but the life of the world

53:30.ar: ذَٰلِكَ مَبۡلَغُهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ
53:30.en: Such is their sum of knowledge. Lo! thy Lord is Best Aware of him who strayeth, and He is Best Aware of him whom goeth right

53:31.ar: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لِيَجۡزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسَٰٓـُٔواْ بِمَا عَمِلُواْ وَيَجۡزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَحۡسَنُواْ بِٱلۡحُسۡنَى
53:31.en: And unto Allah belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, that He may reward those who do evil with that which they have done, and reward those who do good with goodness

53:32.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَجۡتَنِبُونَ كَبَٰٓئِرَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّمَمَۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَٰسِعُ ٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِۚ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِكُمۡ إِذۡ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِذۡ أَنتُمۡ أَجِنَّةࣱ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمۡۖ فَلَا تُزَكُّوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡۖ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰٓ
53:32.en: Those who avoid enormities of sin and abominations, save the unwilled offences - (for them) lo! thy Lord is of vast mercy. He is Best Aware of you (from the time) when He created you from the earth, and when ye were hidden in the bellies of your mothers. Therefor ascribe not purity unto yourselves. He is Best Aware of him who wardeth off (evil)

53:33.en: Didst thou (O Muhammad) observe him who turned away

53:34.en: And gave a little, then was grudging

53:35.en: Hath he knowledge of the Unseen so that he seeth

53:36.ar: أَمۡ لَمۡ يُنَبَّأۡ بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسَىٰ
53:36.en: Or hath he not had news of what is in the books of Moses

53:37.en: And Abraham who paid his debt

53:38.en: That no laden one shall bear another's load

53:39.ar: وَأَن لَّيۡسَ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
53:39.en: And that man hath only that for which he maketh effort

53:40.en: And that his effort will be seen

53:41.en: And afterward he will be repaid for it with fullest payment

53:42.en: And that thy Lord, He is the goal

53:43.en: And that He it is who maketh laugh, and maketh weep

53:44.en: And that He it is Who giveth death and giveth life

53:45.en: And that He createth the two spouses, the male and the female

53:46.en: From a drop (of seed) when it is poured forth

53:47.en: And that He hath ordained the second bringing forth

53:48.en: And that He it is Who enricheth and contenteth

53:49.en: And that He it is Who is the Lord of Sirius

53:50.en: And that He destroyed the former (tribe of) A'ad

53:51.en: And (the tribe of) Thamud He spared not

53:52.ar: وَقَوۡمَ نُوحࣲ مِّن قَبۡلُۖ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ هُمۡ أَظۡلَمَ وَأَطۡغَىٰ
53:52.en: And the folk of Noah aforetime, Lo! they were more unjust and more rebellious

53:54.en: So that there covered them that which did cover

53:55.en: Concerning which then, of the bounties of thy Lord, canst thou dispute

53:56.en: This is a warner of the warners of old

53:58.ar: لَيۡسَ لَهَا مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ
53:58.en: None beside Allah can disclose it

53:59.en: Marvel ye then at this statement

54:1.en: The hour drew nigh and the moon was rent in twain

54:2.ar: وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ ءَايَةࣰ يُعۡرِضُواْ وَيَقُولُواْ سِحۡرࣱ مُّسۡتَمِرࣱّ‏
54:2.en: And if they behold a portent they turn away and say: Prolonged illusion

54:3.ar: وَكَذَّبُواْ وَٱتَّبَعُوٓاْ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡۚ وَكُلُّ أَمۡرࣲ مُّسۡتَقِرࣱّ‏
54:3.en: They denied (the Truth) and followed their own lusts. Yet everything will come to a decision

54:4.ar: وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَنۢبَآءِ مَا فِيهِ مُزۡدَجَرٌ
54:4.en: And surely there hath come unto them news whereof the purport should deter

54:5.en: Effective wisdom; but warnings avail not

54:6.ar: فَتَوَلَّ عَنۡهُمۡۘ يَوۡمَ يَدۡعُ ٱلدَّاعِ إِلَىٰ شَيۡءࣲ نُّكُرٍ
54:6.en: So withdraw from them (O Muhammad) on the day when the Summoner summoneth unto a painful thing

54:7.ar: خُشَّعًا أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمۡ جَرَادࣱ مُّنتَشِرࣱ‏
54:7.en: With downcast eyes, they come forth from the graves as they were locusts spread abroad

54:8.ar: مُّهۡطِعِينَ إِلَى ٱلدَّاعِۖ يَقُولُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا يَوۡمٌ عَسِرࣱ‏
54:8.en: Hastening toward the summoner; the disbelievers say: This is a hard day

54:9.ar: ۞كَذَّبَتۡ قَبۡلَهُمۡ قَوۡمُ نُوحࣲ فَكَذَّبُواْ عَبۡدَنَا وَقَالُواْ مَجۡنُونࣱ وَٱزۡدُجِرَ
54:9.en: The folk of Noah denied before them, yea, they denied Our slave and said: A madman; and he was repulsed

54:10.en: So he cried unto his Lord, saying: I am vanquished, so give help

54:11.en: Then opened We the gates of heaven with pouring water

54:12.ar: وَفَجَّرۡنَا ٱلۡأَرۡضَ عُيُونࣰ ا فَٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡمَآءُ عَلَىٰٓ أَمۡرࣲ قَدۡ قُدِرَ
54:12.en: And caused the earth to gush forth springs, so that the waters met for a predestined purpose

54:13.en: And We carried him upon a thing of planks and nails

54:14.ar: تَجۡرِي بِأَعۡيُنِنَا جَزَآءࣰ لِّمَن كَانَ كُفِرَ
54:14.en: That ran (upon the waters) in Our sight, as a reward for him who was rejected

54:15.ar: وَلَقَد تَّرَكۡنَٰهَآ ءَايَةࣰ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:15.en: And verily We left it as a token; but is there any that remembereth

54:16.en: Then see how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings

54:17.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:17.en: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth

54:18.ar: كَذَّبَتۡ عَادࣱ فَكَيۡفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
54:18.en: (The tribe of) A'ad rejected warnings. Then how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings

54:19.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ رِيحࣰ ا صَرۡصَرࣰ ا فِي يَوۡمِ نَحۡسࣲ مُّسۡتَمِرࣲّ‏
54:19.en: Lo! We let loose on them a raging wind on a day of constant calamity

54:20.ar: تَنزِعُ ٱلنَّاسَ كَأَنَّهُمۡ أَعۡجَازُ نَخۡلࣲ مُّنقَعِرࣲ‏
54:20.en: Sweeping men away as though they were uprooted trunks of palm-trees

54:21.en: Then see how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings

54:22.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:22.en: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth

54:24.ar: فَقَالُوٓاْ أَبَشَرࣰ ا مِّنَّا وَٰحِدࣰ ا نَّتَّبِعُهُۥٓ إِنَّآ إِذࣰ ا لَّفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ وَسُعُرٍ
54:24.en: For they said; Is it a mortal man, alone among us, that we are to follow? Then indeed we should fall into error and madness

54:25.ar: أَءُلۡقِيَ ٱلذِّكۡرُ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۢ بَيۡنِنَا بَلۡ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرࣱ‏
54:25.en: Hath the remembrance been given unto him alone among us? Nay, but he is a rash liar

54:26.ar: سَيَعۡلَمُونَ غَدࣰ ا مَّنِ ٱلۡكَذَّابُ ٱلۡأَشِرُ
54:26.en: (Unto their warner it was said): To-morrow they will know who is the rash liar

54:27.ar: إِنَّا مُرۡسِلُواْ ٱلنَّاقَةِ فِتۡنَةࣰ لَّهُمۡ فَٱرۡتَقِبۡهُمۡ وَٱصۡطَبِرۡ
54:27.en: Lo! We are sending the she-camel as a test for them; so watch them and have patience

54:28.ar: وَنَبِّئۡهُمۡ أَنَّ ٱلۡمَآءَ قِسۡمَةُۢ بَيۡنَهُمۡۖ كُلُّ شِرۡبࣲ مُّحۡتَضَرࣱ‏
54:28.en: And inform them that the water is to be shared between (her and) them. Every drinking will be witnessed

54:29.en: But they call their comrade and he took and hamstrung (her)

54:30.en: Then see how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings

54:31.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ صَيۡحَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ فَكَانُواْ كَهَشِيمِ ٱلۡمُحۡتَظِرِ
54:31.en: Lo! We sent upon them one Shout, and they became as the dry twigs (rejected by) the builder of a cattle-fold

54:32.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:32.en: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth

54:33.en: The folk of Lot rejected warnings

54:34.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ حَاصِبًا إِلَّآ ءَالَ لُوطࣲۖ نَّجَّيۡنَٰهُم بِسَحَرࣲ‏
54:34.en: Lo! We sent a storm of stones upon them (all) save the family of Lot, whom We rescued in the last watch of the night

54:35.ar: نِّعۡمَةࣰ مِّنۡ عِندِنَاۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي مَن شَكَرَ
54:35.en: As grace from Us. Thus We reward him who giveth thanks

54:36.en: And he indeed had warned them of Our blow, but they did doubt the warnings

54:37.ar: وَلَقَدۡ رَٰوَدُوهُ عَن ضَيۡفِهِۦ فَطَمَسۡنَآ أَعۡيُنَهُمۡ فَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
54:37.en: They even asked of him his guests for an ill purpose. Then We blinded their eyes (and said): Taste now My punishment after My warnings

54:38.en: And in truth the punishment decreed befell them early in the morning

54:39.en: Now taste My punishment after My warnings

54:40.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:40.en: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth

54:41.en: And warnings came in truth unto the house of Pharaoh

54:42.ar: كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا كُلِّهَا فَأَخَذۡنَٰهُمۡ أَخۡذَ عَزِيزࣲ مُّقۡتَدِرٍ
54:42.en: Who denied Our revelations, every one. Therefore We grasped them with the grasp of the Mighty, the Powerful

54:43.ar: أَكُفَّارُكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡ أُوْلَٰٓئِكُمۡ أَمۡ لَكُم بَرَآءَةࣱ فِي ٱلزُّبُرِ
54:43.en: Are your disbelievers better than those, or have ye some immunity in the scriptures

54:44.en: Or say they: We are a host victorious

54:45.en: The hosts will all be routed and will turn and flee

54:46.ar: بَلِ ٱلسَّاعَةُ مَوۡعِدُهُمۡ وَٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدۡهَىٰ وَأَمَرُّ
54:46.en: Nay, but the Hour (of doom) is their appointed tryst, and the Hour will be more wretched and more bitter (than their earthly failure)

54:47.en: Lo! the guilty are in error and madness

54:48.ar: يَوۡمَ يُسۡحَبُونَ فِي ٱلنَّارِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمۡ ذُوقُواْ مَسَّ سَقَرَ
54:48.en: On the day when they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces (it is said unto them): Feel the touch of hell

54:49.en: Lo! We have created every thing by measure

54:50.ar: وَمَآ أَمۡرُنَآ إِلَّا وَٰحِدَةࣱ كَلَمۡحِۭ بِٱلۡبَصَرِ
54:50.en: And Our commandment is but one (commandment), as the twinkling of an eye

54:51.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَآ أَشۡيَاعَكُمۡ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:51.en: And verily We have destroyed your fellows; but is there any that remembereth

54:52.en: And every thing they did is in the scriptures

54:53.en: And every small and great thing is recorded

54:54.en: Lo! the righteous will dwell among gardens and rivers

54:55.ar: فِي مَقۡعَدِ صِدۡقٍ عِندَ مَلِيكࣲ مُّقۡتَدِرِۭ
54:55.en: Firmly established in the favour of a Mighty King

55:5.en: The sun and the moon are made punctual

55:6.en: The stars and the trees prostrate

55:7.en: And the sky He hath uplifted; and He hath set the measure

55:8.en: That ye exceed not the measure

55:9.ar: وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلۡوَزۡنَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ وَلَا تُخۡسِرُواْ ٱلۡمِيزَانَ
55:9.en: But observe the measure strictly, nor fall short thereof

55:10.en: And the earth hath He appointed for (His) creatures

55:11.en: Wherein are fruit and sheathed palm-trees

55:13.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

53:62.en: Rather prostrate yourselves before Allah and serve Him

u-5DNWrDKXA.speaker: adnan
u-5DNWrDKXA.speaker_note: his A Juz A Day series; welcomes viewers and teaches throughout in his own voice
u-5DNWrDKXA.title: A Juz A Day: 27th Juz - Allah Gives and Takes As He Pleases
u-5DNWrDKXA.one_line: Adh-Dhariyat, At-Tur, An-Najm, Al-Qamar and the opening of Ar-Rahman: Allah gives and takes as He wills, revelation is real, and punishment and mercy are certain.
u-5DNWrDKXA.summary: He frames the 27th juz around the idea that this is Allah's world: He gives and takes as He pleases. The two winds that open Adh-Dhariyat, one scattering and one carrying rain, illustrate this, followed by the stories of Ibrahim being given a son while the people of Lut, Pharaoh, Ad and Thamud are taken away. He describes the all-round believer who prays at night, seeks forgiveness before dawn, and gives intelligently to both the poor who ask and the poor who do not. At-Tur builds a chain of rhetorical questions that close every escape from the conclusion that Allah alone is worthy of worship, and promises that families of believers are reunited in paradise at the higher rank. In An-Najm he explains how revelation reached the Prophet through Jibril in his true form, ties the Sunnah to revelation, and draws out the core message shared with Musa and Ibrahim: no one carries another's burden and each person gets only what he strove for. Al-Qamar's repeated refrain about the Quran being easy to remember turns the destroyed nations into a question for every listener. He ends at the opening of Ar-Rahman, urging people to read it and connect the favours in the book with the favours around them.

outline.heading: Opening
The surahs of the 27th juz
outline.gist: The juz runs from Adh-Dhariyat to Al-Hadid; he starts from the beginning of Adh-Dhariyat for continuity.

outline.heading: Oaths by the winds: the promise is true
outline.gist: Allah swears by winds, clouds, ships and angels that the Judgment will come; the mockers who ask when it will be are told it is the day of their torment.

outline.heading: Allah gives and Allah takes
outline.gist: The scattering wind and the rain-bearing wind show that Allah grants and withdraws power and provision; realizing the world is not in our control leads to certainty about the Judgment.

outline.heading: Mercy always follows the mention of punishment
outline.gist: The righteous are in gardens and springs; the Quran pairs threat with mercy so we stay hopeful.

outline.heading: The all-round believer: night prayer, dawn forgiveness, smart giving
outline.gist: They sleep little, seek forgiveness before dawn without feeling superior, and give to both the poor who ask and the poor who do not.

outline.heading: As true as the fact that you speak
outline.gist: Human speech, with its genres, law, science and civilization, is unique to us; the revelation is just as certain.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's guests and the roasted calf
outline.gist: Ibrahim hurries to feed strangers and grows afraid when they do not eat, since assassins would refuse a host's food; they give him the news of a knowledgeable son.

outline.heading: Sarah's astonishment and the mission to Lut's people
outline.gist: Sarah wonders at a child in old age; Ibrahim asks the angels' real mission, which is to rain stones on Lut's town after saving its one believing household.

outline.heading: Musa, Ad, Thamud and Nuh: examples of taking away
outline.gist: Pharaoh was cast into the sea, Ad struck by a barren wind and Thamud by a blast, showing Allah takes as He pleases.

outline.heading: An expanding universe, a smoothed earth, pairs of all things
outline.gist: The heavens are built with might and expanding, and the earth is spread out and still beneath us, signs meant to bring awe.

outline.heading: Flee to Allah
outline.gist: Observing creation should produce awe of the Creator and lead to worship of Him alone.

outline.heading: Magician or madman: the same cliche across history
outline.gist: Every nation called its prophet the same names, not by collusion but because transgression produces the same response.

outline.heading: Keep reminding despite the loudmouths
outline.gist: The Prophet is not to blame for their rejection; reminders still benefit believers and those looking for faith.

outline.heading: Created only to worship Him
outline.gist: Allah needs no provision from us; worship is for our benefit, and He alone is the Provider.

outline.heading: What woe means
outline.gist: Wayl is a declaration of destruction, a word that recurs often in the last parts of the Quran.

outline.heading: At-Tur: the punishment is real, and a series of questions
outline.gist: He previews the surah's pattern: a vivid description of punishment and a run of rhetorical questions appealing to reason.

outline.heading: Oaths by the mount, the frequented house and the blazing sea
outline.gist: The house of the angels shows Allah does not need our worship, and the sea set ablaze on the Last Day is something to ponder.

outline.heading: The day of shaking: patient or not, it is the same
outline.gist: Those who amused themselves with falsehood are shoved into the fire, and complaining or enduring makes no difference to their punishment.

outline.heading: The righteous enjoy what their Lord gives
outline.gist: Gardens, bliss and reclining on thrones follow straight after the description of punishment.

outline.heading: Families reunited in paradise
outline.gist: Believing descendants are raised to the rank of their more devoted relatives without reducing anyone's reward, so families are reunited at the higher level.

outline.heading: What got them to paradise: fear and dua
outline.gist: Asked about their lives, the people of paradise say they feared Allah among their families and called on Him alone, a reminder to make dua for ourselves and our families.

outline.heading: Is he a poet? Did they make it up?
outline.gist: The rejection is not a product of intelligent minds but of not wanting to change; if the Quran is invented, let them produce one like it.

outline.heading: Created from nothing, or their own creators?
outline.gist: Each question escalates the impossibility until only one answer remains: Allah created them and alone deserves worship.

outline.heading: Even a falling piece of sky would not convince them
outline.gist: They would call it heaped clouds; Quraysh are warned of punishment in this world before the Judgment.

outline.heading: Be patient: you are under Our eyes
outline.gist: Dawah is a long game; glorify Allah when rising, at night and as the stars fade.

outline.heading: Your companion is not astray and does not speak from whim
outline.gist: The Prophet is someone they knew well; the Quran is Allah's words and the Sunnah in matters of religion is also from revelation, though not worldly matters.

outline.heading: Jibril in his true form on the horizon
outline.gist: The angel who fills the horizon came within two bow lengths; the majesty of the carrier shows the majesty of what he brought.

outline.heading: The second sighting at Sidrat al-Muntaha
outline.gist: During the Isra and Miraj the Prophet saw Jibril again at the furthest edge of creation, and his sight did not waver as he saw great signs.

outline.heading: Al-Lat, Al-Uzza and Manat: names you invented
outline.gist: Assigning daughters to Allah while disliking them is incoherent, and the idols are only inherited assumptions; humans do not get whatever they desire.

outline.heading: The good are rewarded with the best
outline.gist: Evildoers get the consequence of what they did, while doers of good receive the finest reward, far beyond their effort.

outline.heading: Avoid major sins despite minor slips
outline.gist: Small lapses do not cancel greatness; avoiding major and shameful sins does. Allah knew us as foetuses, so do not claim purity for yourselves.

outline.heading: The scriptures of Musa and Ibrahim: only what one strove for
outline.gist: No soul carries another's burden, and a person's life is the sum of their striving, which will be seen and fully rewarded.

outline.heading: He makes us laugh and cry, gives life and death
outline.gist: Joy and sorrow, life and death, wealth and poverty are all from Him; He is Lord of Sirius, the star they worshipped.

outline.heading: Destroyed nations and the same core message
outline.gist: Ad, Thamud, Nuh's people and the overturned cities; the message has always been justice, striving and accountability, and the Hour has drawn near.

outline.heading: Do you laugh instead of weeping? Prostrate
outline.gist: When the Prophet recited the end of An-Najm, even the disbelievers of Quraysh fell into prostration.

outline.heading: Al-Qamar: history as a glimpse of punishment
outline.gist: He points out the refrains about the Quran being easy to remember and how dreadful the punishment was, and the surah's distinctive rhyme.

outline.heading: The moon split and the swarming resurrection
outline.gist: Even the splitting of the moon was called magic; on the Day people will pour from graves like swarming locusts.

outline.heading: Nuh: the gates of the sky opened
outline.gist: Rain poured like an open door and the whole earth became a spring; it was Allah, not planks and nails, that carried the ark.

outline.heading: Ad and the furious wind
outline.gist: People were snatched up and left like uprooted palm trunks; the refrain asks if anyone will take heed.

outline.heading: Thamud and the she-camel
outline.gist: Sent a camel as a test with shared water, they killed it and were flattened by one blast.

outline.heading: Lut's people and Pharaoh's people
outline.gist: A storm of stones for one, while Lut's family was saved before dawn; Pharaoh's people seized in the grip of the Almighty.

outline.heading: Are you better than them, O Makkans?
outline.gist: No immunity is written for them, and their united front would be routed, which happened at Badr, with the Judgment even more bitter.

outline.heading: Everything created in measure; a single word
outline.gist: The order of creation shows it is no accident; every deed is recorded, and the righteous sit in the presence of the Sovereign.

outline.heading: Ar-Rahman: the first surah recited publicly
outline.gist: A companion recited it openly before Quraysh and was beaten nearly to death; its refrain asks which favours you will deny.

outline.heading: He taught the Quran and taught speech; the balance
outline.gist: Speech is a mercy unique to humans; the universe runs on a balance we must not corrupt, so weigh with justice; the earth is for all beings.

outline.heading: Read Ar-Rahman and connect the signs
outline.gist: He urges everyone to read the translation, observe the favours in the book and outside it, and arrive at glorifying the Lord of majesty and honour.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah
themes.note: It is Allah's world: He gives and takes power, provision and life as He wills, which grounds certainty in the Judgment.

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah
themes.note: Laughter and tears, life and death, wealth and poverty all come from Him.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Ibrahim is given a son while Lut's people, Pharaoh, Ad and Thamud are taken away.

themes.label: Quranic stories and their lessons
themes.note: Al-Qamar turns the destroyed nations into a repeated question: will anyone take heed?

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: How revelation reached the Prophet through Jibril in his true form, and why the Sunnah is also from revelation.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: The believer gives intelligently, seeking out the poor who do not ask as well as those who do.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Allah reunites believing families in paradise at the higher rank; the people of paradise feared Allah among their families.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: The people of paradise credit their dua for their salvation, a prompt to pray for ourselves and our families.

themes.label: Agency, responsibility and rejecting victim mentality
themes.note: Each person gets only what he strove for and cannot blame others for his sins.

themes.label: Sins, their causes and remedies
themes.note: Avoiding major and shameful sins is what matters; minor slips do not erase a person's goodness.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The day of shaking and the bliss of the righteous, with mercy always mentioned after punishment.

hadith.gist: When the Prophet recited the end of Surah An-Najm, the disbelievers of Quraysh could not hold back and fell into prostration with the Muslims.

maxims: Allah gives and Allah takes; it is His world
Whenever He mentions punishment, He mentions mercy right after
Don't stop reminding because of a few loudmouths
Your life is the sum of what you strove for
Connect the signs in the book with the signs outside it

stories.who: Ibrahim and his angelic guests
stories.point: His instant generosity to strangers, and Allah giving him a son in old age, illustrate how Allah gives.

stories.who: A companion who first recited Ar-Rahman publicly in Makkah
stories.point: He was beaten almost to death but earned the honour of being the first to recite the Quran openly to Quraysh.

stories.who: Quraysh at Badr
stories.point: The promise that their united front would flee was fulfilled at the Battle of Badr.

contemporary: Expansion of the universe and the stillness of a rotating earth as modern observations matching the verses
takeaways: Accept that power, provision and outcomes are in Allah's hands and live with certainty about the Judgment
Pray at night, seek forgiveness before dawn, and look for the poor who do not ask
Make dua for your family and work toward being reunited with them in paradise
Avoid major and shameful sins and strive, knowing you get only what you work for
Read Ar-Rahman with its translation and connect its favours to the blessings around you

2:183.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
2:183.en: O ye who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you, even as it was prescribed for those before you, that ye may ward off (evil)

2:197.ar: ٱلۡحَجُّ أَشۡهُرࣱ مَّعۡلُومَٰتࣱۚ فَمَن فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ ٱلۡحَجَّ فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّۗ وَمَا تَفۡعَلُواْ مِنۡ خَيۡرࣲ يَعۡلَمۡهُ ٱللَّهُۗ وَتَزَوَّدُواْ فَإِنَّ خَيۡرَ ٱلزَّادِ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُونِ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
2:197.en: The pilgrimage is (in) the well-known months, and whoever is minded to perform the pilgrimage therein (let him remember that) there is (to be) no lewdness nor abuse nor angry conversation on the pilgrimage. And whatsoever good ye do Allah knoweth it. So make provision for yourselves (Hereafter); for the best provision is to ward off evil. Therefore keep your duty unto Me, O men of understanding

7:26.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ قَدۡ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمۡ لِبَاسࣰ ا يُوَٰرِي سَوۡءَٰتِكُمۡ وَرِيشࣰ اۖ وَلِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ ذَٰلِكَ خَيۡرࣱۚ ذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَذَّكَّرُونَ
7:26.en: O Children of Adam! We have revealed unto you raiment to conceal your shame, and splendid vesture, but the raiment of restraint from evil, that is best. This is of the revelations of Allah, that they may remember

9:109.ar: أَفَمَنۡ أَسَّسَ بُنۡيَٰنَهُۥ عَلَىٰ تَقۡوَىٰ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنٍ خَيۡرٌ أَم مَّنۡ أَسَّسَ بُنۡيَٰنَهُۥ عَلَىٰ شَفَا جُرُفٍ هَارࣲ فَٱنۡهَارَ بِهِۦ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
9:109.en: Is he who founded his building upon duty to Allah and His good pleasure better; or he who founded his building on the brink of a crumbling, overhanging precipice so that it toppled with him into the fire of hell? Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

65:2.ar: فَإِذَا بَلَغۡنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَأَمۡسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعۡرُوفٍ أَوۡ فَارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعۡرُوفࣲ وَأَشۡهِدُواْ ذَوَيۡ عَدۡلࣲ مِّنكُمۡ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلشَّهَٰدَةَ لِلَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ يُوعَظُ بِهِۦ مَن كَانَ يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۚ وَمَن يَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ يَجۡعَل لَّهُۥ مَخۡرَجࣰ ا
65:2.en: Then, when they have reached their term, take them back in kindness or part from them in kindness, and call to witness two just men among you, and keep your testimony upright for Allah. Whoso believeth in Allah and the Last Day is exhorted to act thus. And whosoever keepeth his duty to Allah, Allah will appoint a way out for him

65:3.ar: وَيَرۡزُقۡهُ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَا يَحۡتَسِبُۚ وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسۡبُهُۥٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَٰلِغُ أَمۡرِهِۦۚ قَدۡ جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدۡرࣰ ا
65:3.en: And will provide for him from (a quarter) whence he hath no expectation. And whosoever putteth his trust in Allah, He will suffice him. Lo! Allah bringeth His command to pass. Allah hath set a measure for all things

66:6.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ قُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَأَهۡلِيكُمۡ نَارࣰ ا وَقُودُهَا ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلۡحِجَارَةُ عَلَيۡهَا مَلَٰٓئِكَةٌ غِلَاظࣱ شِدَادࣱ لَّا يَعۡصُونَ ٱللَّهَ مَآ أَمَرَهُمۡ وَيَفۡعَلُونَ مَا يُؤۡمَرُونَ
66:6.en: O ye who believe! Ward off from yourselves and your families a Fire whereof the fuel is men and stones, over which are set angels strong, severe, who resist not Allah in that which He commandeth them, but do that which they are commanded

50:19.ar: وَجَآءَتۡ سَكۡرَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ بِٱلۡحَقِّۖ ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنتَ مِنۡهُ تَحِيدُ
50:19.en: And the agony of death cometh in truth. (And it is said unto him): This is that which thou wast wont to shun

3:185.ar: كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۗ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوۡنَ أُجُورَكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۖ فَمَن زُحۡزِحَ عَنِ ٱلنَّارِ وَأُدۡخِلَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ فَقَدۡ فَازَۗ وَمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡغُرُورِ
3:185.en: Every soul will taste of death. And ye will be paid on the Day of Resurrection only that which ye have fairly earned. Whoso is removed from the Fire and is made to enter paradise, he indeed is triumphant. The life of this world is but comfort of illusion

21:34.ar: وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا لِبَشَرࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ ٱلۡخُلۡدَۖ أَفَإِيْن مِّتَّ فَهُمُ ٱلۡخَٰلِدُونَ
21:34.en: We appointed immortality for no mortal before thee. What! if thou diest, can they be immortal

21:35.ar: كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۗ وَنَبۡلُوكُم بِٱلشَّرِّ وَٱلۡخَيۡرِ فِتۡنَةࣰۖ وَإِلَيۡنَا تُرۡجَعُونَ
21:35.en: Every soul must taste of death, and We try you with evil and with good, for ordeal. And unto Us ye will be returned

39:30.en: Lo! thou wilt die, and lo! they will die

4:78.ar: أَيۡنَمَا تَكُونُواْ يُدۡرِككُّمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ وَلَوۡ كُنتُمۡ فِي بُرُوجࣲ مُّشَيَّدَةࣲۗ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ حَسَنَةࣱ يَقُولُواْ هَٰذِهِۦ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَيِّئَةࣱ يَقُولُواْ هَٰذِهِۦ مِنۡ عِندِكَۚ قُلۡ كُلࣱّ مِّنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَالِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ لَا يَكَادُونَ يَفۡقَهُونَ حَدِيثࣰ ا
4:78.en: Wheresoever ye may be, death will overtake you, even though ye were in lofty towers. Yet if a happy thing befalleth them they say: This is from Allah; and if an evil thing befalleth them they say: This is of thy doing (O Muhammad). Say (unto them): All is from Allah. What is amiss with these people that they come not nigh to understand a happening

23:99.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَهُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ قَالَ رَبِّ ٱرۡجِعُونِ
23:99.en: Until, when death cometh unto one of them, he saith: My Lord! Send me back

23:100.ar: لَعَلِّيٓ أَعۡمَلُ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فِيمَا تَرَكۡتُۚ كَلَّآۚ إِنَّهَا كَلِمَةٌ هُوَ قَآئِلُهَاۖ وَمِن وَرَآئِهِم بَرۡزَخٌ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ يُبۡعَثُونَ
23:100.en: That I may do right in that which I have left behind! But nay! It is but a word that he speaketh; and behind them is a barrier until the day when they are raised

39:67.ar: وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدۡرِهِۦ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ جَمِيعࣰ ا قَبۡضَتُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ مَطۡوِيَّٰتُۢ بِيَمِينِهِۦۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
39:67.en: And they esteem not Allah as He hath the right to be esteemed, when the whole earth is His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens are rolled in His right hand. Glorified is He and High Exalted from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)

39:68.ar: وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَصَعِقَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَّا مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُۖ ثُمَّ نُفِخَ فِيهِ أُخۡرَىٰ فَإِذَا هُمۡ قِيَامࣱ يَنظُرُونَ
39:68.en: And the trumpet is blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are in the earth swoon away, save him whom Allah willeth. Then it is blown a second time, and behold them standing waiting

22:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمۡۚ إِنَّ زَلۡزَلَةَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ شَيۡءٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
22:1.en: O mankind! Fear your Lord. Lo! the earthquake of the Hour (of Doom) is a tremendous thing

22:2.ar: يَوۡمَ تَرَوۡنَهَا تَذۡهَلُ كُلُّ مُرۡضِعَةٍ عَمَّآ أَرۡضَعَتۡ وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ ذَاتِ حَمۡلٍ حَمۡلَهَا وَتَرَى ٱلنَّاسَ سُكَٰرَىٰ وَمَا هُم بِسُكَٰرَىٰ وَلَٰكِنَّ عَذَابَ ٱللَّهِ شَدِيدࣱ‏
22:2.en: On the day when ye behold it, every nursing mother will forget her nursling and every pregnant one will be delivered of her burden, and thou (Muhammad) wilt see mankind as drunken, yet they will not be drunken, but the Doom of Allah will be strong (upon them)

53:58.ar: لَيۡسَ لَهَا مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ
53:58.en: None beside Allah can disclose it

53:59.en: Marvel ye then at this statement

50:41.ar: وَٱسۡتَمِعۡ يَوۡمَ يُنَادِ ٱلۡمُنَادِ مِن مَّكَانࣲ قَرِيبࣲ‏
50:41.en: And listen on the day when the crier crieth from a near place

50:42.ar: يَوۡمَ يَسۡمَعُونَ ٱلصَّيۡحَةَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ ذَٰلِكَ يَوۡمُ ٱلۡخُرُوجِ
50:42.en: The day when they will hear the (Awful) Cry in truth. That is the day of coming forth (from the graves)

54:7.ar: خُشَّعًا أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمۡ جَرَادࣱ مُّنتَشِرࣱ‏
54:7.en: With downcast eyes, they come forth from the graves as they were locusts spread abroad

54:8.ar: مُّهۡطِعِينَ إِلَى ٱلدَّاعِۖ يَقُولُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا يَوۡمٌ عَسِرࣱ‏
54:8.en: Hastening toward the summoner; the disbelievers say: This is a hard day

20:105.ar: وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡجِبَالِ فَقُلۡ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسۡفࣰ ا
20:105.en: They will ask thee of the mountains (on that day). Say: My Lord will break them into scattered dust

20:106.en: And leave it as an empty plain

20:107.ar: لَّا تَرَىٰ فِيهَا عِوَجࣰ ا وَلَآ أَمۡتࣰ ا
20:107.en: Wherein thou seest neither curve nor ruggedness

23:112.ar: قَٰلَ كَمۡ لَبِثۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ عَدَدَ سِنِينَ
23:112.en: He will say: How long tarried ye in the earth, counting by years

23:113.ar: قَالُواْ لَبِثۡنَا يَوۡمًا أَوۡ بَعۡضَ يَوۡمࣲ فَسۡـَٔلِ ٱلۡعَآدِّينَ
23:113.en: They will say: We tarried by a day or part of a day. Ask of those who keep count

23:114.ar: قَٰلَ إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ اۖ لَّوۡ أَنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
23:114.en: He will say: Ye tarried but a little if ye only knew

40:16.ar: يَوۡمَ هُم بَٰرِزُونَۖ لَا يَخۡفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِنۡهُمۡ شَيۡءࣱۚ لِّمَنِ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۖ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡوَٰحِدِ ٱلۡقَهَّارِ
40:16.en: The day when they come forth, nothing of them being hidden from Allah. Whose is the Sovereignty this day? It is Allah's, the One, the Almighty

18:100.en: On that day we shall present hell to the disbelievers, plain to view

18:101.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ كَانَتۡ أَعۡيُنُهُمۡ فِي غِطَآءٍ عَن ذِكۡرِي وَكَانُواْ لَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ سَمۡعًا
18:101.en: Those whose eyes were hoodwinked from My reminder, and who could not bear to hear

89:23.ar: وَجِاْيٓءَ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بِجَهَنَّمَۚ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ ٱلذِّكۡرَىٰ
89:23.en: And hell is brought near that day; on that day man will remember, but how will the remembrance (then avail him)

70:11.ar: يُبَصَّرُونَهُمۡۚ يَوَدُّ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُ لَوۡ يَفۡتَدِي مِنۡ عَذَابِ يَوۡمِئِذِۭ بِبَنِيهِ
70:11.en: Though they will be given sight of them. The guilty man will long to be able to ransom himself from the punishment of that day at the price of his children

70:12.en: And his spouse and his brother

70:13.en: And his kin that harboured him

70:14.ar: وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
70:14.en: And all that are in the earth, if then it might deliver him

25:12.ar: إِذَا رَأَتۡهُم مِّن مَّكَانِۭ بَعِيدࣲ سَمِعُواْ لَهَا تَغَيُّظࣰ ا وَزَفِيرࣰ ا
25:12.en: When it seeth them from afar, they hear the crackling and the roar thereof

77:32.en: Lo! it throweth up sparks like the castles

45:28.ar: وَتَرَىٰ كُلَّ أُمَّةࣲ جَاثِيَةࣰۚ كُلُّ أُمَّةࣲ تُدۡعَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ كِتَٰبِهَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُجۡزَوۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
45:28.en: And thou wilt see each nation crouching, each nation summoned to its record. (And it will be said unto them): This day ye are requited what ye used to do

23:107.ar: رَبَّنَآ أَخۡرِجۡنَا مِنۡهَا فَإِنۡ عُدۡنَا فَإِنَّا ظَٰلِمُونَ
23:107.en: Our Lord! Oh, bring us forth from hence! If we return (to evil) then indeed we shall be wrong-doers

18:49.ar: وَوُضِعَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ فَتَرَى ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ مُشۡفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ وَيَقُولُونَ يَٰوَيۡلَتَنَا مَالِ هَٰذَا ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةࣰ وَلَا كَبِيرَةً إِلَّآ أَحۡصَىٰهَاۚ وَوَجَدُواْ مَا عَمِلُواْ حَاضِرࣰ اۗ وَلَا يَظۡلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:49.en: And the Book is placed, and thou seest the guilty fearful of that which is therein, and they say: What kind of a Book is this that leaveth not a small thing nor a great thing but hath counted it! And they find all that they did confronting them, and thy Lord wrongeth no-one

17:14.ar: ٱقۡرَأۡ كِتَٰبَكَ كَفَىٰ بِنَفۡسِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكَ حَسِيبࣰ ا
17:14.en: (And it will be said unto him): Read thy Book. Thy soul sufficeth as reckoner against thee this day

84:10.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ وَرَآءَ ظَهۡرِهِۦ
84:10.en: But whoso is given his account behind his back

89:22.ar: وَجَآءَ رَبُّكَ وَٱلۡمَلَكُ صَفࣰّ ا صَفࣰّ ا
89:22.en: And thy Lord shall come with angels, rank on rank

69:17.ar: وَٱلۡمَلَكُ عَلَىٰٓ أَرۡجَآئِهَاۚ وَيَحۡمِلُ عَرۡشَ رَبِّكَ فَوۡقَهُمۡ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ ثَمَٰنِيَةࣱ‏
69:17.en: And the angels will be on the sides thereof, and eight will uphold the Throne of thy Lord that day, above them

68:42.ar: يَوۡمَ يُكۡشَفُ عَن سَاقࣲ وَيُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ فَلَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ
68:42.en: On the day when it befalleth in earnest, and they are ordered to prostrate themselves but are not able

68:43.ar: خَٰشِعَةً أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ تَرۡهَقُهُمۡ ذِلَّةࣱۖ وَقَدۡ كَانُواْ يُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ وَهُمۡ سَٰلِمُونَ
68:43.en: With eyes downcast, abasement stupefying them. And they had been summoned to prostrate themselves while they were yet unhurt

19:71.ar: وَإِن مِّنكُمۡ إِلَّا وَارِدُهَاۚ كَانَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ حَتۡمࣰ ا مَّقۡضِيࣰّ ا
19:71.en: There is not one of you but shall approach it. That is a fixed ordinance of thy Lord

57:13.ar: يَوۡمَ يَقُولُ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقَٰتُ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱنظُرُونَا نَقۡتَبِسۡ مِن نُّورِكُمۡ قِيلَ ٱرۡجِعُواْ وَرَآءَكُمۡ فَٱلۡتَمِسُواْ نُورࣰ اۖ فَضُرِبَ بَيۡنَهُم بِسُورࣲ لَّهُۥ بَابُۢ بَاطِنُهُۥ فِيهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةُ وَظَٰهِرُهُۥ مِن قِبَلِهِ ٱلۡعَذَابُ
57:13.en: On the day when the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women will say unto those who believe: Look on us that we may borrow from your light! it will be said: Go back and seek for light! Then there will separate them a wall wherein is a gate, the inner side whereof containeth mercy, while the outer side thereof is toward the doom

pvIzOXvSCUU.speaker: adnan
pvIzOXvSCUU.speaker_note: two voices: a guest doctor and the sheikh alternate on taqwa until 43:00; the sheikh alone leads the tawahhum exercise from 46:33
pvIzOXvSCUU.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 27: Operationalizing Taqwa and a Tawahhum Exercise
pvIzOXvSCUU.one_line: A practical definition of taqwa applied to money, time and family, followed by a guided contemplation from the deathbed to the final verdict.
pvIzOXvSCUU.summary: The night has two parts. First, in conversation with a guest physician, he treats taqwa as the goal of fasting and asks how to make it measurable. Taqwa is the baseline, not the summit: asking whether something will displease Allah, or whether you will regret it, and braking when the answer is yes, like steering around slush or a car's lane assist. It can only be measured in oneself, and Ramadan removes the usual excuses. The Quran attaches taqwa to the hardest situations, such as fasting and divorce, as a safety valve, and prevention always beats seeking forgiveness afterwards. They apply it to zakat season (riba, shady investments, unpaid debts, withheld inheritance, complicit employers), to time and screen use, where the sheikh notes an hour a day adds up to years, to social media algorithms, and to the home, where family members know a person's real taqwa. Second, the sheikh leads a tawahhum exercise of guided reflection: the angel of death, the departing soul, the grave and its doors, the two blasts of the horn, resurrection, the gathering in sweat, the seven shaded by the Throne, Jahannam paraded, the books, the prostration, the Prophet's basin, the bridge, and standing before Allah for the verdict, with la ilaha illa Allah as the refrain. He asks people to repeat this reflection for a few minutes daily.

outline.heading: Opening
Why do we fast? To gain taqwa
outline.gist: The guest asks the audience why we fast and lands on the verse: fasting was prescribed so that we may attain taqwa.

outline.heading: Operationalizing taqwa: each Ramadan better than the last
outline.gist: The guest says an objective must be made measurable; the test is whether each Ramadan starts higher than the last, so the last is the best.

outline.heading: Defining taqwa: the thorny path
outline.gist: Taqwa is usually defined with words as vague as itself; a companion asked for its meaning answered with a question about walking a path full of thorns.

outline.heading: The Eid sneakers in the slush
outline.gist: The guest updates the image: walking to Eid prayer in prized new shoes, you step around every puddle.

outline.heading: Taqwa as lane assist
outline.gist: Taqwa nudges you back when you drift across Allah's limits; push hard enough and desire overrides it.

outline.heading: Taqwa is the baseline, not the summit
outline.gist: Defining it in lofty terms makes people give up; taqwa is practical and is the minimum standard.

outline.heading: Two questions: will it please or displease Allah?
outline.gist: Asking whether every act pleases Allah is the level of the elite; taqwa only asks whether it displeases Him, then hits the brakes.

outline.heading: The permissible gray zone and preventive character
outline.gist: Most of life is mubah and allowed; taqwa means protection, like preventive medicine for the soul.

outline.heading: Pilgrims who set out without provisions
outline.gist: People of Yemen went to hajj taking nothing, saying Allah will feed us, and died on the way; the Quran told them to take provision, for the best provision is taqwa.

outline.heading: Ask before every step: will I regret this?
outline.gist: Slowing down to ask whether you will regret something here or before Allah is taqwa made operational; aim higher later.

outline.heading: No taqwa meters: flip the camera to yourself
outline.gist: The guest says taqwa was meant as a front-facing camera for self-assessment, but people turned it on everyone else, even children judging others in salah.

outline.heading: Ramadan as the ultimate spiritual selfie
outline.gist: With shaytan chained and everyone on best behaviour, Ramadan removes the excuses, so it is the month to assess yourself.

outline.heading: Taqwa across the Quran
outline.gist: The root appears around 256 times, as the outcome of worship, as a command and as a condition for achievement.

outline.heading: Taqwa as food, clothing and shelter
outline.gist: Allah describes it as provision, as a garment and as a foundation for a building; missing its meaning means missing much of the Quran.

outline.heading: Compare these days to your normal days
outline.gist: Less distraction, less social media, more good deeds: Ramadan shows how much better life is with taqwa.

outline.heading: Taqwa attached to the hardest acts: fasting
outline.gist: Hajj is hard for a few days, but fasting brings weeks of anxiety beforehand, which is why taqwa is tied to it.

outline.heading: Divorce and the page with the most taqwa
outline.gist: Divorce is the hardest social situation, and the opening of At-Talaq mentions taqwa more than any page because that is when you need it most.

outline.heading: Taqwa as the safety valve
outline.gist: When you have lost yourself you can always fall back on one simple question and step away.

outline.heading: You can only measure your own
outline.gist: Count how many decisions today you slowed down for and whether you chose well; judging others' taqwa is none of your business.

outline.heading: Prevention beats damage control
outline.gist: Avoiding the wrong is better ten times out of ten than seeking forgiveness and fatwas afterwards; youth who learn this get far ahead.

outline.heading: Deflection in hard conversations
outline.gist: The guest notes most marital arguments involve justifying or deflecting, the same reflex we use to avoid self-assessment.

outline.heading: 'Worry about yourself': the worst reply
outline.gist: The guest cites the hadith that the worst speech is answering 'fear Allah' with 'mind yourself'.

outline.heading: Three areas to apply taqwa
outline.gist: The guest proposes family relationships, finances and provision as areas to operationalize taqwa.

outline.heading: Provision: where we show the least taqwa
outline.gist: Because income feels vital, people take riba, gray investments, tax shortcuts and benefit claims; Allah promises provision from unexpected places to the mindful.

outline.heading: A way out of financial strain
