outline.gist: The promise comes in At-Talaq because divorce causes itemized financial strain, much like the Western context.

outline.heading: Zakat season: audit your wealth
outline.gist: Having just reviewed accounts for zakat, check whether investments are Sharia compliant, whether you owe unpaid debts, and whether a sister's inheritance was withheld.

outline.heading: Zakat is not a blanket purifier
outline.gist: Paying two and a half percent does not clean whatever shady dealings the rest of the wealth carries.

outline.heading: Is your employer a bank or complicit in war?
outline.gist: The guest asks people to consider whether their workplace deals in riba or supports the war on fellow Muslims; Allah promises a better way out.

outline.heading: For the young, taqwa shows in time
outline.gist: Taqwa matters most in the capital you have most of, and for young people that is time.

outline.heading: Reading out your screen time
outline.gist: He polls the room on the weekly phone usage report, as he does in his mentorship program, and finds few under several hours a day.

outline.heading: An hour a day is two years by sixty
outline.gist: Six or eight hours a day would add up to a decade staring at a phone, even granting work and Quran use.

outline.heading: Build on Ramadan's better distribution
outline.gist: Even if total screen time held steady, more of it went to Quran; carry that forward.

outline.heading: One device for guidance and for everything else
outline.gist: The guest asks how the same vessel used to read the Quran can carry everything else.

outline.heading: The attention economy
outline.gist: Platforms keep you scrolling to sell ads and push constant upward comparisons about homes, skin, bodies, cars and spouses.

outline.heading: Train your algorithm
outline.gist: The guest says the algorithm mirrors your lowest self; use Ramadan's taqwa to reshape it, since music and worse slip in through every reel.

outline.heading: Numbing is not self-care
outline.gist: Scrolling gets rebranded as self-care; mark content not interested, block and unfollow.

outline.heading: Haram but make it Muslim
outline.gist: Muslim influencer content often trades on attraction and showing off spouses, accepted because of a beard or hijab.

outline.heading: Retrain it on Mondays and Thursdays
outline.gist: An incognito feed shows how platforms bait attention; voluntary fasts are a good time to clean the feed again.

outline.heading: Your family holds your taqwa meter
outline.gist: The guest says people may smile in the masjid and scowl at home; family members see what you watch and how you behave.

outline.heading: Taqwa starts at home
outline.gist: Protect yourselves and your families; the shepherd is responsible, and the best of people are the best to their families.

outline.heading: Interlude
An exercise of reflection, not an act of worship
outline.gist: The tawahhum exercise needs complete silence; it is contemplation, not a sunnah ritual, though contemplation is central to the deen.

outline.heading: Walking through the stations of the hereafter
outline.gist: He narrates the Quran- and sunnah-based journey after death station by station, with ten tahlils between stations, while listeners imagine themselves at its centre.

outline.heading: Practise it a few minutes daily
outline.gist: Reflecting on verses about death and judgment has a profound effect on behaviour, closeness to Allah and taqwa.

outline.heading: Interlude
The angel of death arrives
outline.gist: A creature no one else sees sits at your head with companions in white or otherwise; you cannot speak and the stupor of death comes with truth.

outline.heading: Remembering your choices
outline.gist: Lying there you recall your regrets and the people you wronged, gripped by sadness or calm depending on your direction.

outline.heading: Every soul shall taste death
outline.gist: Verses on death's certainty: no one was granted immortality, the Prophet too would die, and death finds you even in fortified towers.

outline.heading: Calm soul or wicked soul
outline.gist: The angel addresses you by your name and your father's name, calling the soul out to Allah's mercy or to His wrath.

outline.heading: The spirit leaves the body
outline.gist: Numbness rises from the feet, regrets flood in, and all you can hope for is that your tongue says la ilaha illa Allah.

outline.heading: 'Send me back' and the barzakh
outline.gist: The dying beg to return and do good; the answer is no, and a barrier stands until resurrection.

outline.heading: How the soul departs
outline.gist: A good soul slips out like a drop from a spout, a bad one like a dry branch pulled from damp wool, and is wrapped in a shroud from paradise or the Fire.

outline.heading: The grave and the soul's ascent
outline.gist: The grave is the first station: if you pass it what follows is easier; the soul is carried up, the heavens open or stay shut, and it is praised or scorned.

outline.heading: Truly alone for the first time
outline.gist: Even the womb had warmth; the grave is tight and dark, and doors open onto paradise and onto Jahannam.

outline.heading: One door closes forever
outline.gist: You spend your time in the grave looking through the door that stays open, either longing for the Hour or dreading it.

outline.heading: Your deeds keep you company; the three questions
outline.gist: Prayer, zakat and fasting sit around you to shield you, and you are asked about your Lord, your Prophet and your religion.

outline.heading: Only one phrase saves you in the grave
outline.gist: Whatever you prepared, the testimony of faith is what rescues you there.

outline.heading: The first blast of the horn
outline.gist: Humanity, still arguing and debating, waits for a single blast from the angel created for it.

outline.heading: It comes without warning
outline.gist: A man repairing an appliance, another lifting food to his mouth, two people haggling over a garment: none finish.

outline.heading: The earth folded in His hand
outline.gist: They did not revere Allah as He deserves; the earth and heavens are in His grip, and the blast ends all life, even in the graves.

outline.heading: The last angels die
outline.gist: The angel of death takes the hornblower, then Jibril, then his own soul, until no one remains.

outline.heading: 'I am the King: where are the kings?'
outline.gist: Allah alone, as He always was, calls into the void asking where the kings and tyrants of the earth are.

outline.heading: The second blast: resurrection
outline.gist: Life rushes into everything that ever lived and your consciousness returns in the grave.

outline.heading: The quake of the Hour
outline.gist: Nursing mothers forget their infants, pregnancies end, and people look drunk from fear.

outline.heading: The approaching Hour and the caller
outline.gist: Do you laugh rather than weep at this news? Everyone answers the caller who calls from a near place.

outline.heading: Your body recreated
outline.gist: After ages in the earth your veins, nerves and skin are rebuilt exactly as you remember, and you brush off the dust.

outline.heading: Fleeing familiar faces
outline.gist: You see siblings, parents, children and friends, and people run so their eyes do not fall on faces that remind them of their wrongs.

outline.heading: Locusts in every direction, families holding hands
outline.gist: Most run in fear toward the caller, but some families stand together calmly, strengthening one another.

outline.heading: The universe crumbles
outline.gist: The sun is rolled up, stars fall, and mountains are marched off and blown into dust.

outline.heading: Witnessing what you always knew
outline.gist: Everything Allah described is now in front of you, and the only true word left is the testimony of faith.

outline.heading: The flat white land of judgment
outline.gist: No hills, valleys, rocks or shade, nowhere to hide and nothing to put between you and others.

outline.heading: Unclothed and searching for cover
outline.gist: You suddenly notice you are naked, as is everyone, and all you want is something to cover yourself.

outline.heading: Coverings of different lengths
outline.gist: Some trail long garments, some barely cover themselves, and whether your faults are covered depends on your choices.

outline.heading: How people arrive at the gathering
outline.gist: Some ride, some walk, some are dragged on their faces, some are tiny as ants, some sit on pedestals of light with loved ones.

outline.heading: How long did you stay on earth?
outline.gist: They say a day or part of a day, and are told they lived only a little, if only they had known.

outline.heading: The sun brought near and the sea of sweat
outline.gist: Sweat rises to ankles, waists or mouths according to deeds, and people search for relief.

outline.heading: Shade of the Throne, by invitation only
outline.gist: A shade appears on the horizon, but humanity is stopped and names are called.

outline.heading: First of the seven: just leaders
outline.gist: Just rulers are called into the shade.

outline.heading: Second of the seven: youth raised in worship
outline.gist: Young people who spent their best years serving Allah are called.

outline.heading: Third of the seven: hearts attached to the masjid
outline.gist: Those who cannot wait to return to the masjid are called.

outline.heading: Fourth of the seven: love for Allah's sake
outline.gist: Pairs who met and parted for Allah walk toward the shade.

outline.heading: Fifth of the seven: resisting temptation
outline.gist: Those offered haram who refused are called, and very few move.

outline.heading: Sixth of the seven: secret charity
outline.gist: Those whose left hand did not know what the right gave are called.

outline.heading: Seventh of the seven: tears in private
outline.gist: Those who remembered Allah alone and wept are called, and each group leaves chanting the testimony of joy. Are you still standing in the sweat?

outline.heading: The rumbling and the call of sovereignty
outline.gist: The earth shakes, nothing is hidden, and the call rings out: to whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.

outline.heading: Jahannam paraded before the disbelievers
outline.gist: It is displayed to those whose eyes were veiled from remembrance; people remember everything, too late.

outline.heading: Taken before the judgment begins
outline.gist: Some are plucked from the crowd into the Fire before any reckoning, and you ask what they did.

outline.heading: First thrown: the reciter
outline.gist: He claims he recited for Allah and is told he recited to be called a reciter.

outline.heading: Second thrown: the scholar
outline.gist: He learned so people would call him a scholar, and they did.

outline.heading: Third thrown: the martyr
outline.gist: He fought to be called brave, and he was.

outline.heading: Fourth thrown: the philanthropist
outline.gist: He gave to be called generous among his peers, and he was.

outline.heading: Ransoming with one's own family
outline.gist: Seeing Jahannam, people offer their children, spouses, siblings, kin and everyone on earth in their place.

outline.heading: The fury of Jahannam
outline.gist: Its roar is heard from afar, sparks fly like castles, and it is held by seventy thousand reins, each with seventy thousand angels.

outline.heading: Knees that buckle
outline.gist: Everyone falls to their knees, glancing sideways at a fire kindled for thousands of years until it turned black.

outline.heading: 'Our Lord, bring us out'
outline.gist: From inside comes the plea to be returned to do right, and everyone watching can only say la ilaha illa Allah.

outline.heading: The books fly to their owners
outline.gist: Like a thousand arrows on the horizon, every record heads to its owner, and the guilty despair at its detail.

outline.heading: Read your book
outline.gist: Nothing small or great is left out, your Lord wrongs no one, and you are told to be your own accountant.

outline.heading: Right hand, left hand or behind the back
outline.gist: Those who know their book will come in the left hand hide it behind them, and it lands there anyway.

outline.heading: Your Lord comes with the angels
outline.gist: Rows of angels fill every corner, and eight mighty angels carry the Throne.

outline.heading: The call to prostrate
outline.gist: Some fall into sujud in honour; others find their backs rigid as metal because they refused to prostrate in life, and no one can help them.

outline.heading: Interlude
The basin seen from afar
outline.gist: Thirsty and exhausted, you approach a crowd gathered around a great basin of water purer than silver.

outline.heading: The Prophet at his basin
outline.gist: It smells better than musk, is whiter than snow and sweeter than honey, with cups like stars, and the man you heard of all your life stands there.

outline.heading: Seeing his face for the first time
outline.gist: You push through the crowd toward the most beautiful smile you have ever seen as he fills cup after cup.

outline.heading: Turned away from the basin
outline.gist: An angel blocks a man from the cup; the Prophet pleads that he is of his ummah and is told he does not know what they changed after him.

outline.heading: Your turn at the basin
outline.gist: He promised to meet you at the basin; you extend your hand hoping no barrier comes between you and the cup.

outline.heading: The cliff of Jahannam and the bridge
outline.gist: Everyone comes to a cliff so deep a stone falls for seventy years, with a path across it finer than a hair.

outline.heading: Crossing like lightning, wind or step by step
outline.gist: People cross at the speed of their deeds, as they walked the path of the deen in this life.

outline.heading: The light you carry
outline.gist: Hypocrites beg the believers to wait so they can borrow light and are told to go back and seek it; a wall comes between them.

outline.heading: Hooks along the bridge
outline.gist: Hooks snatch at people in proportion to what they took in this world; some freeze, some crawl, and one drops just before reaching the far side.

outline.heading: The Prophet's intercession and the hundred mercies
outline.gist: He prostrates beneath the Throne asking mercy for his ummah, and Allah joins the one mercy He sent to earth with His ninety-nine.

outline.heading: Reading your book before the scales
outline.gist: The reckoning begins, and the more you read, the more you wish things were not there.

outline.heading: Waiting for your name
outline.gist: You watch others celebrated or dragged away until you are called to stand in the court where only justice is served.

outline.heading: Standing before Allah
outline.gist: Reading your book aloud, you hope to rush past what shames you; if fortunate He accepts your apology quickly.

outline.heading: Awaiting the verdict
outline.gist: No earlier pain or joy compares to the word that decides the rest of your existence.

outline.heading: The only word with the weight to save you
outline.gist: The angels tell you that la ilaha illa Allah alone carries the weight to save you that day.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Taqwa and God-consciousness
themes.note: Taqwa is the baseline question of whether an act displeases Allah or will be regretted, applied as a brake before acting.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Taqwa can only be measured in oneself; turning it on others and deflecting criticism are the common failures.

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: Divorce is the hardest social situation, which is why At-Talaq repeats taqwa so often.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Provision is where people show the least taqwa: riba, gray investments, unpaid debts, withheld inheritance and complicit employers.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: The zakat audit is a chance to examine all of one's wealth, not a blanket purification of it.

themes.label: Time, opportunity and seizing the moment
themes.note: For the young, time is the capital where taqwa shows; an hour a day becomes years of a life.

themes.label: Technology, AI, social media and attention
themes.note: Screen time, the attention economy and algorithms that mirror the lowest self; retrain the feed as you train the nafs.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Family members see a person's real taqwa; it starts at home with protecting oneself and one's family.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: Contemplation is a central but neglected practice; a few minutes a day of reflecting on death changes behaviour.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: The deathbed, the angel of death, the departing soul and the solitude of the grave, narrated for personal reflection.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The horn, resurrection, the gathering, the shade, Jahannam, the books, the basin, the bridge and the verdict, with the testimony of faith as the only rescue.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: The reciter, scholar, martyr and philanthropist who acted for reputation are the first thrown into the Fire.

quran.point: Fasting was prescribed so that you may attain taqwa.
Take provision for hajj, and the best provision is taqwa.
The garment of taqwa is the best garment.
A building founded on taqwa: taqwa as shelter.
Whoever has taqwa, Allah makes a way out for him and provides from where he does not expect.
Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire.
The stupor of death comes with the truth: what you were avoiding.
Every soul shall taste death.
No human before you was granted immortality; if you die, will they live forever?
You will die and they will die.
Death will reach you even in lofty towers.
The dying beg to be sent back; behind them is a barrier until resurrection.
They did not revere Allah as He deserves; the earth in His grip and the blast of the horn.
The quake of the Hour makes nursing mothers forget their infants.
The approaching Hour has drawn near; do you laugh and not weep?
The caller calls from a near place and all hear the blast in truth.
They come out like scattered locusts, rushing toward the caller.
The sun is wrapped up and the stars fall.
Allah will blast the mountains to dust and leave a level plain with no crookedness.
How long did you remain on earth? A day or part of a day.
To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.
Jahannam is displayed to those whose eyes were veiled from remembrance.
On that day man will remember, but what use is remembering then?
The criminal would ransom himself with his children, spouse, brother, kin and everyone on earth.
When it sees them from afar they hear its fury and roaring.
It throws sparks as huge as castles.
Every nation will be seen kneeling.
Our Lord, bring us out; if we return we would be wrongdoers.
What is this book that leaves nothing small or great unrecorded? Your Lord wrongs no one.
Read your book; you suffice today as your own accountant.
Whoever is given his book behind his back.
Your Lord comes with the angels rank upon rank.
Eight angels carry the Throne of your Lord that day.
They are called to prostrate and cannot, having been called when they were able.
There is none of you but will come to it.
The hypocrites ask the believers to wait so they may borrow their light and are told to go back and seek it.

hadith.gist: A companion asked about taqwa replied by asking whether he had walked a thorny path and how he gathered himself to avoid the thorns.
The worst speech is when a man is told 'fear Allah' and replies 'mind yourself'.
The best of you are the best to their families, and I am the best of you to my family.

The angel of death sits at the head of the dying and calls the good soul out to Allah's forgiveness and pleasure and the wicked soul to His wrath; the good soul flows out like a drop from a waterskin, the other is dragged like a skewer through wet wool.
The grave is the first station of the hereafter; whoever is saved from it finds what follows easier.
In the grave prayer stands at the head, zakat at the right and fasting at the left to shield the believer.
The Hour will come while two men have spread a garment between them and not finished their sale, and a man raises food to his mouth and does not eat it.
Allah will fold the heavens and the earth and say: I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?
On the Day of Resurrection people will be in sweat according to their deeds, to their ankles, knees, waists or mouths.

Seven are shaded by Allah on the day there is no shade but His: the just ruler, the youth raised in worship, the one attached to the masjid, two who love for Allah, the one who refuses temptation, the secret giver and the one who weeps remembering Allah alone.
The first judged and thrown into the Fire are a reciter, a scholar, a martyr and a generous man who acted to be praised.
Jahannam is brought with seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels.
The Fire was kindled a thousand years until red, a thousand until white and a thousand until black.
The Prophet's basin is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey with cups as many as the stars; some will be driven away and he will be told he does not know what they changed after him.
On the bridge people pass like lightning, wind and swift horses, with hooks that snatch them.
Allah has a hundred mercies; He sent one to earth and kept ninety-nine for the Day of Resurrection.

H747NSOgt-4.summary: This recording of Fajr on 17 March 2026 is prayer only. It is the Fajr prayer that concludes the Ramadan completion of the Quran, recited with Al-Kafirun, An-Nasr and Al-Masad in the first rakah and Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas in the second, followed by the traditional dua of khatm al-Quran (asking that the Quran be the spring of the hearts, a proof for and not against the worshippers, and a means of mercy for parents and teachers) and duas for the oppressed in Palestine, Syria and Sudan. No reminder or talk is given.

67:1.ar: تَبَٰرَكَ ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
67:1.en: Blessed is He in Whose hand is the Sovereignty, and, He is Able to do all things

67:2.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ أَيُّكُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلࣰ اۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفُورُ
67:2.en: Who hath created life and death that He may try you which of you is best in conduct; and He is the Mighty, the Forgiving

67:3.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲ طِبَاقࣰ اۖ مَّا تَرَىٰ فِي خَلۡقِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ مِن تَفَٰوُتࣲۖ فَٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ هَلۡ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورࣲ‏
67:3.en: Who hath created seven heavens in harmony. Thou (Muhammad) canst see no fault in the Beneficent One's creation; then look again: Canst thou see any rifts

67:4.ar: ثُمَّ ٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيۡنِ يَنقَلِبۡ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡبَصَرُ خَاسِئࣰ ا وَهُوَ حَسِيرࣱ‏
67:4.en: Then look again and yet again, thy sight will return unto thee weakened and made dim

67:5.ar: وَلَقَدۡ زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا بِمَصَٰبِيحَ وَجَعَلۡنَٰهَا رُجُومࣰ ا لِّلشَّيَٰطِينِۖ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لَهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:5.en: And verily We have beautified the world's heaven with lamps, and We have made them missiles for the devils, and for them We have prepared the doom of flame

67:6.ar: وَلِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّهِمۡ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
67:6.en: And for those who disbelieve in their Lord there is the doom of hell, a hapless journey's end

67:7.ar: إِذَآ أُلۡقُواْ فِيهَا سَمِعُواْ لَهَا شَهِيقࣰ ا وَهِيَ تَفُورُ
67:7.en: When they are flung therein they hear its roaring as it boileth up

67:8.ar: تَكَادُ تَمَيَّزُ مِنَ ٱلۡغَيۡظِۖ كُلَّمَآ أُلۡقِيَ فِيهَا فَوۡجࣱ سَأَلَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَآ أَلَمۡ يَأۡتِكُمۡ نَذِيرࣱ‏
67:8.en: As it would burst with rage. Whenever a (fresh) host is flung therein the wardens thereof ask them: Came there unto you no warner

67:9.ar: قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ قَدۡ جَآءَنَا نَذِيرࣱ فَكَذَّبۡنَا وَقُلۡنَا مَا نَزَّلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ كَبِيرࣲ‏
67:9.en: They say: Yea, verily, a warner came unto us; but we denied and said: Allah hath naught revealed; ye are in naught but a great error

67:10.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡ كُنَّا نَسۡمَعُ أَوۡ نَعۡقِلُ مَا كُنَّا فِيٓ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:10.en: And they say: Had we been wont to listen or have sense, we had not been among the dwellers in the flames

67:11.ar: فَٱعۡتَرَفُواْ بِذَنۢبِهِمۡ فَسُحۡقࣰ ا لِّأَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:11.en: So they acknowledge their sins; but far removed (from mercy) are the dwellers in the flames

67:12.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣱ وَأَجۡرࣱ كَبِيرࣱ‏
67:12.en: Lo! those who fear their Lord in secret, theirs will be forgiveness and a great reward

67:13.ar: وَأَسِرُّواْ قَوۡلَكُمۡ أَوِ ٱجۡهَرُواْ بِهِۦٓۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
67:13.en: And keep your opinion secret or proclaim it, lo! He is Knower of all that is in the breasts (of men)

67:14.ar: أَلَا يَعۡلَمُ مَنۡ خَلَقَ وَهُوَ ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
67:14.en: Should He not know what He created? And He is the Subtile, the Aware

67:15.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ ذَلُولࣰ ا فَٱمۡشُواْ فِي مَنَاكِبِهَا وَكُلُواْ مِن رِّزۡقِهِۦۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلنُّشُورُ
67:15.en: He it is Who hath made the earth subservient unto you, so Walk in the paths thereof and eat of His providence. And unto Him will be the resurrection (of the dead)

67:16.ar: ءَأَمِنتُم مَّن فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يَخۡسِفَ بِكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَمُورُ
67:16.en: Have ye taken security from Him Who is in the heaven that He will not cause the earth to swallow you when lo! it is convulsed

67:17.ar: أَمۡ أَمِنتُم مَّن فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يُرۡسِلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حَاصِبࣰ اۖ فَسَتَعۡلَمُونَ كَيۡفَ نَذِيرِ
67:17.en: Or have ye taken security from Him Who is in the heaven that He will not let loose on you a hurricane? But ye shall know the manner of My warning

67:18.ar: وَلَقَدۡ كَذَّبَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ فَكَيۡفَ كَانَ نَكِيرِ
67:18.en: And verily those before them denied, then (see) the manner of My wrath (with them)

67:19.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ إِلَى ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَوۡقَهُمۡ صَٰٓفَّٰتࣲ وَيَقۡبِضۡنَۚ مَا يُمۡسِكُهُنَّ إِلَّا ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُۚ إِنَّهُۥ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءِۭ بَصِيرٌ
67:19.en: Have they not seen the birds above them spreading out their wings and closing them? Naught upholdeth them save the Beneficent. Lo! He is Seer of all things

67:20.ar: أَمَّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ جُندࣱ لَّكُمۡ يَنصُرُكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِۚ إِنِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ إِلَّا فِي غُرُورٍ
67:20.en: Or who is he that will be an army unto you to help you instead of the Beneficent? The disbelievers are in naught but illusion

67:21.ar: أَمَّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي يَرۡزُقُكُمۡ إِنۡ أَمۡسَكَ رِزۡقَهُۥۚ بَل لَّجُّواْ فِي عُتُوࣲّ وَنُفُورٍ
67:21.en: Or who is he that will provide for you if He should withhold His providence? Nay, but they are set in pride and frowardness

67:22.ar: أَفَمَن يَمۡشِي مُكِبًّا عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦٓ أَهۡدَىٰٓ أَمَّن يَمۡشِي سَوِيًّا عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
67:22.en: Is he who goeth groping on his face more rightly guided, or he who walketh upright on a straight road

67:23.ar: قُلۡ هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنشَأَكُمۡ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرَ وَٱلۡأَفۡـِٔدَةَۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تَشۡكُرُونَ
67:23.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): He it is who gave you being, and hath assigned unto you ears and eyes and hearts. Small thanks give ye

67:24.ar: قُلۡ هُوَ ٱلَّذِي ذَرَأَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
67:24.en: Say: He it is Who multiplieth you in the earth, and unto Whom ye will be gathered

67:25.ar: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلۡوَعۡدُ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
67:25.en: And they say: When (will) this promise (be fulfilled), if ye are truthful

67:26.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّمَا ٱلۡعِلۡمُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَإِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
67:26.en: Say: The knowledge is with Allah only, and I am but a plain warner

67:27.ar: فَلَمَّا رَأَوۡهُ زُلۡفَةࣰ سِيٓـَٔتۡ وُجُوهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَقِيلَ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَدَّعُونَ
67:27.en: But when they see it nigh, the faces of those who disbelieve will be awry, and it will be said (unto them): This is that for which ye used to call

67:28.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِنۡ أَهۡلَكَنِيَ ٱللَّهُ وَمَن مَّعِيَ أَوۡ رَحِمَنَا فَمَن يُجِيرُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ مِنۡ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
67:28.en: Say (O Muhammad): Have ye thought: Whether Allah causeth me (Muhammad) and those with me to perish or hath mercy on us, still, who will protect the disbelievers from a painful doom

67:29.ar: قُلۡ هُوَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ وَعَلَيۡهِ تَوَكَّلۡنَاۖ فَسَتَعۡلَمُونَ مَنۡ هُوَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
67:29.en: Say: He is the Beneficent. In Him we believe and in Him we put our trust. And ye will soon know who it is that is in error manifest

67:30.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِنۡ أَصۡبَحَ مَآؤُكُمۡ غَوۡرࣰ ا فَمَن يَأۡتِيكُم بِمَآءࣲ مَّعِينِۭ
67:30.en: Say: Have ye thought: If (all) your water were to disappear into the earth, who then could bring you gushing water

68:1.en: Nun. By the pen and that which they write (therewith)

68:2.en: Thou art not, for thy Lord's favour unto thee, a madman

68:3.en: And lo! thine verily will be a reward unfailing

68:4.en: And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature

68:5.en: And thou wilt see and they will see

68:6.en: Which of you is the demented

68:7.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِٱلۡمُهۡتَدِينَ
68:7.en: Lo! thy Lord is Best Aware of him who strayeth from His way, and He is Best Aware of those who walk aright

68:8.en: Therefor obey not thou the rejecters

68:9.en: Who would have had thee compromise, that they may compromise

68:10.en: Neither obey thou each feeble oath-monger

68:12.en: Hinderer of the good, transgressor, malefactor

68:14.en: It is because he is possessed of wealth and children

68:15.ar: إِذَا تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِ ءَايَٰتُنَا قَالَ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
68:15.en: That, when Our revelations are recited unto him, he saith: Mere fables of the men of old

68:16.en: We shall brand him on the nose

68:17.ar: إِنَّا بَلَوۡنَٰهُمۡ كَمَا بَلَوۡنَآ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ إِذۡ أَقۡسَمُواْ لَيَصۡرِمُنَّهَا مُصۡبِحِينَ
68:17.en: Lo! We have tried them as We tried the owners of the garden when they vowed that they would pluck its fruit next morning

68:18.en: And made no exception (for the Will of Allah)

68:19.ar: فَطَافَ عَلَيۡهَا طَآئِفࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمۡ نَآئِمُونَ
68:19.en: Then a visitation from thy Lord came upon it while they slept

68:20.en: And in the morning it was as if plucked

68:21.en: And they cried out one unto another in the morning

68:22.ar: أَنِ ٱغۡدُواْ عَلَىٰ حَرۡثِكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰرِمِينَ
68:22.en: Saying: Run unto your field if ye would pluck (the fruit)

68:23.en: So they went off, saying one unto another in low tones

68:24.ar: أَن لَّا يَدۡخُلَنَّهَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّسۡكِينࣱ‏
68:24.en: No needy man shall enter it to-day against you

68:25.en: They went betimes, strong in (this) purpose

68:26.en: But when they saw it, they said: Lo! we are in error

68:28.ar: قَالَ أَوۡسَطُهُمۡ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ لَوۡلَا تُسَبِّحُونَ
68:28.en: The best among them said: Said I not unto you: Why glorify ye not (Allah)

68:29.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
68:29.en: They said: Glorified be our Lord! Lo! we have been wrong-doers

68:30.en: Then some of them drew near unto others, self-reproaching

68:31.en: They said: Alas for us! In truth we were outrageous

68:32.ar: عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَآ أَن يُبۡدِلَنَا خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهَآ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَٰغِبُونَ
68:32.en: It may be that our Lord will give us better than this in place thereof. Lo! we beseech our Lord

68:33.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡعَذَابُۖ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ أَكۡبَرُۚ لَوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ
68:33.en: Such was the punishment. And verily the punishment of the Hereafter is greater if they did but know

68:34.ar: إِنَّ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ جَنَّٰتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
68:34.en: Lo! for those who keep from evil are gardens of bliss with their Lord

68:35.en: Shall We then treat those who have surrendered as We treat the guilty

68:36.en: What aileth you? How foolishly ye judge

68:37.en: Or have ye a scripture wherein ye learn

68:38.en: That ye shall indeed have all that ye choose

68:39.ar: أَمۡ لَكُمۡ أَيۡمَٰنٌ عَلَيۡنَا بَٰلِغَةٌ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّ لَكُمۡ لَمَا تَحۡكُمُونَ
68:39.en: Or have ye a covenant on oath from Us that reacheth to the Day of Judgment, that yours shall be all that ye ordain

68:40.en: Ask them (O Muhammad) which of them will vouch for that

68:41.ar: أَمۡ لَهُمۡ شُرَكَآءُ فَلۡيَأۡتُواْ بِشُرَكَآئِهِمۡ إِن كَانُواْ صَٰدِقِينَ
68:41.en: Or have they other gods? Then let them bring their other gods if they are truthful

68:42.ar: يَوۡمَ يُكۡشَفُ عَن سَاقࣲ وَيُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ فَلَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ
68:42.en: On the day when it befalleth in earnest, and they are ordered to prostrate themselves but are not able

68:43.ar: خَٰشِعَةً أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ تَرۡهَقُهُمۡ ذِلَّةࣱۖ وَقَدۡ كَانُواْ يُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ وَهُمۡ سَٰلِمُونَ
68:43.en: With eyes downcast, abasement stupefying them. And they had been summoned to prostrate themselves while they were yet unhurt

68:44.ar: فَذَرۡنِي وَمَن يُكَذِّبُ بِهَٰذَا ٱلۡحَدِيثِۖ سَنَسۡتَدۡرِجُهُم مِّنۡ حَيۡثُ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
68:44.en: Leave Me (to deal) with those who give the lie to this pronouncement. We shall lead them on by steps from whence they know not

68:45.en: Yet I bear with them, for lo! My scheme is firm

68:46.ar: أَمۡ تَسۡـَٔلُهُمۡ أَجۡرࣰ ا فَهُم مِّن مَّغۡرَمࣲ مُّثۡقَلُونَ
68:46.en: Or dost thou (Muhammad) ask a fee from them so that they are heavily taxed

68:47.en: Or is the Unseen theirs that they can write (thereof)

68:48.ar: فَٱصۡبِرۡ لِحُكۡمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلۡحُوتِ إِذۡ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكۡظُومࣱ‏
68:48.en: But wait thou for thy Lord's decree, and be not like him of the fish, who cried out in despair

68:49.ar: لَّوۡلَآ أَن تَدَٰرَكَهُۥ نِعۡمَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ لَنُبِذَ بِٱلۡعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ مَذۡمُومࣱ‏
68:49.en: Had it not been that favour from his Lord had reached him he surely had been cast into the wilderness while he was reprobate

68:50.en: But his Lord chose him and placed him among the righteous

68:51.ar: وَإِن يَكَادُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَيُزۡلِقُونَكَ بِأَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ لَمَّا سَمِعُواْ ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُۥ لَمَجۡنُونࣱ‏
68:51.en: And lo! those who disbelieve would fain disconcert thee with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say: Lo! he is indeed mad

68:52.en: When it is naught else than a Reminder to creation

69:3.en: Ah, what will convey unto thee what the reality is

69:4.en: (The tribes of) Thamud and A'ad disbelieved in the judgment to come

69:5.en: As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the lightning

69:6.ar: وَأَمَّا عَادࣱ فَأُهۡلِكُواْ بِرِيحࣲ صَرۡصَرٍ عَاتِيَةࣲ‏
69:6.en: And as for A'ad, they were destroyed by a fierce roaring wind

69:7.ar: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ سَبۡعَ لَيَالࣲ وَثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومࣰ اۖ فَتَرَى ٱلۡقَوۡمَ فِيهَا صَرۡعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمۡ أَعۡجَازُ نَخۡلٍ خَاوِيَةࣲ‏
69:7.en: Which He imposed on them for seven long nights and eight long days so that thou mightest have seen men lying overthrown, as they were hollow trunks of palm-trees

69:8.en: Canst thou (O Muhammad) see any remnant of them

69:9.ar: وَجَآءَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ وَمَن قَبۡلَهُۥ وَٱلۡمُؤۡتَفِكَٰتُ بِٱلۡخَاطِئَةِ
69:9.en: And Pharaoh and those before him, and the communities that were destroyed, brought error

69:10.ar: فَعَصَوۡاْ رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمۡ فَأَخَذَهُمۡ أَخۡذَةࣰ رَّابِيَةً
69:10.en: And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, therefor did He grip them with a tightening grip

69:11.ar: إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَا ٱلۡمَآءُ حَمَلۡنَٰكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡجَارِيَةِ
69:11.en: Lo! when the waters rose, We carried you upon the ship

69:12.ar: لِنَجۡعَلَهَا لَكُمۡ تَذۡكِرَةࣰ وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنࣱ وَٰعِيَةࣱ‏
69:12.en: That We might make it a memorial for you, and that remembering ears (that heard the story) might remember

69:13.ar: فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ نَفۡخَةࣱ وَٰحِدَةࣱ‏
69:13.en: And when the trumpet shall sound one blast

69:14.ar: وَحُمِلَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَٱلۡجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ‏
69:14.en: And the earth with the mountains shall be lifted up and crushed with one crash

69:15.en: Then, on that day will the Event befall

69:16.en: And the heaven will split asunder, for that day it will be frail

69:17.ar: وَٱلۡمَلَكُ عَلَىٰٓ أَرۡجَآئِهَاۚ وَيَحۡمِلُ عَرۡشَ رَبِّكَ فَوۡقَهُمۡ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ ثَمَٰنِيَةࣱ‏
69:17.en: And the angels will be on the sides thereof, and eight will uphold the Throne of thy Lord that day, above them

69:18.ar: يَوۡمَئِذࣲ تُعۡرَضُونَ لَا تَخۡفَىٰ مِنكُمۡ خَافِيَةࣱ‏
69:18.en: On that day ye will be exposed; not a secret of you will be hidden

69:19.ar: فَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ هَآؤُمُ ٱقۡرَءُواْ كِتَٰبِيَهۡ
69:19.en: Then, as for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: Take, read my book

69:20.en: Surely I knew that I should have to meet my reckoning

69:21.en: Then he will be in blissful state

69:23.en: Whereof the clusters are in easy reach

69:24.ar: كُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ هَنِيٓـَٔۢا بِمَآ أَسۡلَفۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَيَّامِ ٱلۡخَالِيَةِ
69:24.en: (And it will be said unto those therein): Eat and drink at ease for that which ye sent on before you in past days

69:25.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِشِمَالِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي لَمۡ أُوتَ كِتَٰبِيَهۡ
69:25.en: But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say: Oh, would that I had not been given my book

69:26.en: And knew not what my reckoning

69:27.en: Oh, would that it had been death

69:28.en: My wealth hath not availed me

69:29.en: My power hath gone from me

69:30.en: (It will be said): Take him and fetter him

69:31.en: And then expose him to hell-fire

69:32.ar: ثُمَّ فِي سِلۡسِلَةࣲ ذَرۡعُهَا سَبۡعُونَ ذِرَاعࣰ ا فَٱسۡلُكُوهُ
69:32.en: And then insert him in a chain whereof the length is seventy cubits

69:33.ar: إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
69:33.en: Lo! He used not to believe in Allah the Tremendous

69:34.en: And urged not on the feeding of the wretched

69:35.en: Therefor hath he no lover here this day

69:38.en: But nay! I swear by all that ye see

69:39.en: And all that ye see not

69:40.en: That it is indeed the speech of an illustrious messenger

69:41.ar: وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوۡلِ شَاعِرࣲۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تُؤۡمِنُونَ
69:41.en: It is not poet's speech - little is it that ye believe

69:42.ar: وَلَا بِقَوۡلِ كَاهِنࣲۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ
69:42.en: Nor diviner's speech - little is it that ye remember

69:43.en: It is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds

69:44.en: And if he had invented false sayings concerning Us

69:45.en: We assuredly had taken him by the right hand

69:47.ar: فَمَا مِنكُم مِّنۡ أَحَدٍ عَنۡهُ حَٰجِزِينَ
69:47.en: And not one of you could have held Us off from him

69:48.en: And lo! it is a warrant unto those who ward off (evil)

69:49.en: And lo! We know that some among you will deny (it)

69:50.en: And lo! it is indeed an anguish for the disbelievers

69:51.en: And lo! it is absolute truth

69:52.en: So glorify the name of thy Tremendous Lord

70:1.en: A questioner questioned concerning the doom about to fall

70:2.en: Upon the disbelievers, which none can repel

70:3.en: From Allah, Lord of the Ascending Stairways

70:4.ar: تَعۡرُجُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيۡهِ فِي يَوۡمࣲ كَانَ مِقۡدَارُهُۥ خَمۡسِينَ أَلۡفَ سَنَةࣲ‏
70:4.en: (Whereby) the angels and the Spirit ascend unto Him in a Day whereof the span is fifty thousand years

70:5.en: But be patient (O Muhammad) with a patience fair to see

70:6.en: Lo! they behold it afar off

70:8.en: The day when the sky will become as molten copper

70:9.en: And the hills become as flakes of wool

70:10.en: And no familiar friend will ask a question of his friend

70:11.ar: يُبَصَّرُونَهُمۡۚ يَوَدُّ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُ لَوۡ يَفۡتَدِي مِنۡ عَذَابِ يَوۡمِئِذِۭ بِبَنِيهِ
70:11.en: Though they will be given sight of them. The guilty man will long to be able to ransom himself from the punishment of that day at the price of his children

70:12.en: And his spouse and his brother

70:13.en: And his kin that harboured him

70:14.ar: وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
70:14.en: And all that are in the earth, if then it might deliver him

70:15.en: But nay! for lo! it is the fire of hell

70:17.en: It calleth him who turned and fled (from truth)

70:21.en: And, when good befalleth him, grudging

70:23.en: Who are constant at their worship

70:24.en: And in whose wealth there is a right acknowledged

70:25.en: For the beggar and the destitute

70:26.en: And those who believe in the Day of Judgment

70:27.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم مِّنۡ عَذَابِ رَبِّهِم مُّشۡفِقُونَ
70:27.en: And those who are fearful of their Lord's doom

70:28.en: Lo! the doom of their Lord is that before which none can feel secure

70:29.en: And those who preserve their chastity

70:30.ar: إِلَّا عَلَىٰٓ أَزۡوَٰجِهِمۡ أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُمۡ فَإِنَّهُمۡ غَيۡرُ مَلُومِينَ
70:30.en: Save with their wives and those whom their right hands possess, for thus they are not blameworthy

70:31.ar: فَمَنِ ٱبۡتَغَىٰ وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡعَادُونَ
70:31.en: But whoso seeketh more than that, those are they who are transgressors

70:32.en: And those who keep their pledges and their covenant

70:33.en: And those who stand by their testimony

70:34.en: And those who are attentive at their worship

70:35.en: These will dwell in Gardens, honoured

70:36.en: What aileth those who disbelieve, that they keep staring toward thee (O Muhammad), open-eyed

70:37.en: On the right and on the left, in groups

70:38.ar: أَيَطۡمَعُ كُلُّ ٱمۡرِيࣲٕ مِّنۡهُمۡ أَن يُدۡخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمࣲ‏
70:38.en: Doth every man among them hope to enter the Garden of Delight

70:39.en: Nay, verily. Lo! We created them from what they know

70:40.ar: فَلَآ أُقۡسِمُ بِرَبِّ ٱلۡمَشَٰرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغَٰرِبِ إِنَّا لَقَٰدِرُونَ
70:40.en: But nay! I swear by the Lord of the rising-places and the setting-places of the planets that We verily are Able

70:41.ar: عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّبَدِّلَ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمَسۡبُوقِينَ
70:41.en: To replace them by (others) better than them. And we are not to be outrun

70:42.ar: فَذَرۡهُمۡ يَخُوضُواْ وَيَلۡعَبُواْ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُواْ يَوۡمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ
70:42.en: So let them chat and play until they meet their Day which they are promised

70:43.ar: يَوۡمَ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ سِرَاعࣰ ا كَأَنَّهُمۡ إِلَىٰ نُصُبࣲ يُوفِضُونَ
70:43.en: The day when they come forth from the graves in haste, as racing to a goal

70:44.ar: خَٰشِعَةً أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ تَرۡهَقُهُمۡ ذِلَّةࣱۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمُ ٱلَّذِي كَانُواْ يُوعَدُونَ
70:44.en: With eyes aghast, abasement stupefying them: Such is the Day which they are promised

71:1.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦٓ أَنۡ أَنذِرۡ قَوۡمَكَ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
71:1.en: Lo! We sent Noah unto his people (saying): Warn thy people ere the painful doom come unto them

71:2.ar: قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنِّي لَكُمۡ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينٌ
71:2.en: He said: O my people! Lo! I am a plain warner unto you

71:3.en: (Bidding you): Serve Allah and keep your duty unto Him and obey me

71:4.ar: يَغۡفِرۡ لَكُم مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمۡ وَيُؤَخِّرۡكُمۡ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ مُّسَمًّىۚ إِنَّ أَجَلَ ٱللَّهِ إِذَا جَآءَ لَا يُؤَخَّرُۚ لَوۡ كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
71:4.en: That He may forgive you somewhat of your sins and respite you to an appointed term. Lo! the term of Allah, when it cometh, cannot be delayed, if ye but knew

71:5.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوۡتُ قَوۡمِي لَيۡلࣰ ا وَنَهَارࣰ ا
71:5.en: He said: My Lord! Lo! I have called unto my people night and day

71:6.ar: فَلَمۡ يَزِدۡهُمۡ دُعَآءِيٓ إِلَّا فِرَارࣰ ا
71:6.en: But all my calling doth but add to their repugnance

71:7.ar: وَإِنِّي كُلَّمَا دَعَوۡتُهُمۡ لِتَغۡفِرَ لَهُمۡ جَعَلُوٓاْ أَصَٰبِعَهُمۡ فِيٓ ءَاذَانِهِمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡشَوۡاْ ثِيَابَهُمۡ وَأَصَرُّواْ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ ٱسۡتِكۡبَارࣰ ا
71:7.en: And lo! whenever I call unto them that Thou mayst pardon them they thrust their fingers in their ears and cover themselves with their garments and persist (in their refusal) and magnify themselves in pride

71:8.en: And lo! I have called unto them aloud

71:9.ar: ثُمَّ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَنتُ لَهُمۡ وَأَسۡرَرۡتُ لَهُمۡ إِسۡرَارࣰ ا
71:9.en: And lo! I have made public proclamation unto them, and I have appealed to them in private

71:10.ar: فَقُلۡتُ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفَّارࣰ ا
71:10.en: And I have said: Seek pardon of your Lord. Lo! He was ever Forgiving

71:11.en: He will let loose the sky for you in plenteous rain

71:12.ar: وَيُمۡدِدۡكُم بِأَمۡوَٰلࣲ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ أَنۡهَٰرࣰ ا
71:12.en: And will help you with wealth and sons, and will assign unto you Gardens and will assign unto you rivers

71:13.ar: مَّا لَكُمۡ لَا تَرۡجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَارࣰ ا
71:13.en: What aileth you that ye hope not toward Allah for dignity

71:14.en: When He created you by (divers) stages

71:15.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَوۡاْ كَيۡفَ خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲ طِبَاقࣰ ا
71:15.en: See ye not how Allah hath created seven heavens in harmony

71:16.ar: وَجَعَلَ ٱلۡقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورࣰ ا وَجَعَلَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ سِرَاجࣰ ا
71:16.en: And hath made the moon a light therein, and made the sun a lamp

71:17.ar: وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ نَبَاتࣰ ا
71:17.en: And Allah hath caused you to grow as a growth from the earth

71:18.ar: ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمۡ فِيهَا وَيُخۡرِجُكُمۡ إِخۡرَاجࣰ ا
71:18.en: And afterward He maketh you return thereto, and He will bring you forth again, a (new) forthbringing

71:19.ar: وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِسَاطࣰ ا
71:19.en: And Allah hath made the earth a wide expanse for you

71:20.ar: لِّتَسۡلُكُواْ مِنۡهَا سُبُلࣰ ا فِجَاجࣰ ا
71:20.en: That ye may thread the valley-ways thereof

71:21.ar: قَالَ نُوحࣱ رَّبِّ إِنَّهُمۡ عَصَوۡنِي وَٱتَّبَعُواْ مَن لَّمۡ يَزِدۡهُ مَالُهُۥ وَوَلَدُهُۥٓ إِلَّا خَسَارࣰ ا
71:21.en: Noah said: My Lord! Lo! they have disobeyed me and followed one whose wealth and children increase him in naught save ruin

71:22.en: And they have plotted a mighty plot

71:23.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَا تَذَرُنَّ ءَالِهَتَكُمۡ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدࣰّ ا وَلَا سُوَاعࣰ ا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسۡرࣰ ا
71:23.en: And they have said: Forsake not your gods. Forsake not Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr

71:24.ar: وَقَدۡ أَضَلُّواْ كَثِيرࣰ اۖ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلَٰلࣰ ا
71:24.en: And they have led many astray, and Thou increasest the wrong-doers in naught save error

71:25.ar: مِّمَّا خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِهِمۡ أُغۡرِقُواْ فَأُدۡخِلُواْ نَارࣰ ا فَلَمۡ يَجِدُواْ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَنصَارࣰ ا
71:25.en: Because of their sins they were drowned, then made to enter a Fire. And they found they had no helpers in place of Allah

71:26.ar: وَقَالَ نُوحࣱ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرۡ عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ دَيَّارًا
71:26.en: And Noah said: My Lord! Leave not one of the disbelievers in the land

71:27.ar: إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرۡهُمۡ يُضِلُّواْ عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوٓاْ إِلَّا فَاجِرࣰ ا كَفَّارࣰ ا
71:27.en: If Thou shouldst leave them, they will mislead Thy slaves and will beget none save lewd ingrates

71:28.ar: رَّبِّ ٱغۡفِرۡ لِي وَلِوَٰلِدَيَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيۡتِيَ مُؤۡمِنࣰ ا وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِۖ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارَۢا
71:28.en: My Lord! Forgive me and my parents and him who entereth my house believing, and believing men and believing women, and increase not the wrong-doers in aught save ruin

72:1.ar: قُلۡ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ ٱسۡتَمَعَ نَفَرࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا سَمِعۡنَا قُرۡءَانًا عَجَبࣰ ا
72:1.en: Say (O Muhammad): It is revealed unto me that a company of the Jinn gave ear, and they said: Lo! we have heard a marvellous Qur'an

72:2.ar: يَهۡدِيٓ إِلَى ٱلرُّشۡدِ فَـَٔامَنَّا بِهِۦۖ وَلَن نُّشۡرِكَ بِرَبِّنَآ أَحَدࣰ ا
72:2.en: Which guideth unto righteousness, so we believe in it and we ascribe no partner unto our Lord

72:3.ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ تَعَٰلَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا مَا ٱتَّخَذَ صَٰحِبَةࣰ وَلَا وَلَدࣰ ا
72:3.en: And (we believe) that He - exalted be the glory of our Lord! - hath taken neither wife nor son

72:4.ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ كَانَ يَقُولُ سَفِيهُنَا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ شَطَطࣰ ا
72:4.en: And that the foolish one among us used to speak concerning Allah an atrocious lie

72:5.ar: وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن تَقُولَ ٱلۡإِنسُ وَٱلۡجِنُّ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبࣰ ا
72:5.en: And lo! we had supposed that humankind and jinn would not speak a lie concerning Allah

72:6.ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ كَانَ رِجَالࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡإِنسِ يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجَالࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ فَزَادُوهُمۡ رَهَقࣰ ا
72:6.en: And indeed (O Muhammad) individuals of humankind used to invoke the protection of individuals of the jinn, so that they increased them in revolt against Allah

72:7.ar: وَأَنَّهُمۡ ظَنُّواْ كَمَا ظَنَنتُمۡ أَن لَّن يَبۡعَثَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدࣰ ا
72:7.en: And indeed they supposed, even as ye suppose, that Allah would not raise anyone (from the dead)

72:8.ar: وَأَنَّا لَمَسۡنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ فَوَجَدۡنَٰهَا مُلِئَتۡ حَرَسࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ ا وَشُهُبࣰ ا
72:8.en: And (the Jinn who had listened to the Qur'an said): We had sought the heaven but had found it filled with strong warders and meteors

72:9.ar: وَأَنَّا كُنَّا نَقۡعُدُ مِنۡهَا مَقَٰعِدَ لِلسَّمۡعِۖ فَمَن يَسۡتَمِعِ ٱلۡأٓنَ يَجِدۡ لَهُۥ شِهَابࣰ ا رَّصَدࣰ ا
72:9.en: And we used to sit on places (high) therein to listen. But he who listeneth now findeth a flame in wait for him

72:10.ar: وَأَنَّا لَا نَدۡرِيٓ أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ بِمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَمۡ أَرَادَ بِهِمۡ رَبُّهُمۡ رَشَدࣰ ا
72:10.en: And we know not whether harm is boded unto all who are in the earth, or whether their Lord intendeth guidance for them

72:11.ar: وَأَنَّا مِنَّا ٱلصَّٰلِحُونَ وَمِنَّا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَۖ كُنَّا طَرَآئِقَ قِدَدࣰ ا
72:11.en: And among us there are righteous folk and among us there are far from that. We are sects having different rules

72:12.ar: وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن نُّعۡجِزَ ٱللَّهَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَن نُّعۡجِزَهُۥ هَرَبࣰ ا
72:12.en: And we know that we cannot escape from Allah in the earth, nor can we escape by flight

72:13.ar: وَأَنَّا لَمَّا سَمِعۡنَا ٱلۡهُدَىٰٓ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦۖ فَمَن يُؤۡمِنۢ بِرَبِّهِۦ فَلَا يَخَافُ بَخۡسࣰ ا وَلَا رَهَقࣰ ا
72:13.en: And when we heard the guidance, we believed therein, and whoso believeth in his Lord, he feareth neither loss nor oppression

72:14.ar: وَأَنَّا مِنَّا ٱلۡمُسۡلِمُونَ وَمِنَّا ٱلۡقَٰسِطُونَۖ فَمَنۡ أَسۡلَمَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ تَحَرَّوۡاْ رَشَدࣰ ا
72:14.en: And there are among us some who have surrendered (to Allah) and there are among us some who are unjust. And whoso hath surrendered to Allah, such have taken the right path purposefully

72:15.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلۡقَٰسِطُونَ فَكَانُواْ لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَبࣰ ا
72:15.en: And as for those who are unjust, they are firewood for hell

72:16.ar: وَأَلَّوِ ٱسۡتَقَٰمُواْ عَلَى ٱلطَّرِيقَةِ لَأَسۡقَيۡنَٰهُم مَّآءً غَدَقࣰ ا
72:16.en: If they (the idolaters) tread the right path, We shall give them to drink of water in abundance

72:17.ar: لِّنَفۡتِنَهُمۡ فِيهِۚ وَمَن يُعۡرِضۡ عَن ذِكۡرِ رَبِّهِۦ يَسۡلُكۡهُ عَذَابࣰ ا صَعَدࣰ ا
72:17.en: That We may test them thereby, and whoso turneth away from the remembrance of his Lord; He will thrust him into ever-growing torment

72:18.ar: وَأَنَّ ٱلۡمَسَٰجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلَا تَدۡعُواْ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ أَحَدࣰ ا
72:18.en: And the places of worship are only for Allah, so pray not unto anyone along with Allah

72:19.ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ لَمَّا قَامَ عَبۡدُ ٱللَّهِ يَدۡعُوهُ كَادُواْ يَكُونُونَ عَلَيۡهِ لِبَدࣰ ا
72:19.en: And when the slave of Allah stood up in prayer to Him, they crowded on him, almost stifling

72:20.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَدۡعُواْ رَبِّي وَلَآ أُشۡرِكُ بِهِۦٓ أَحَدࣰ ا
72:20.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): I pray unto Allah only, and ascribe unto Him no partner

72:21.ar: قُلۡ إِنِّي لَآ أَمۡلِكُ لَكُمۡ ضَرࣰّ ا وَلَا رَشَدࣰ ا
72:21.en: Say: Lo! I control not hurt nor benefit for you

72:22.ar: قُلۡ إِنِّي لَن يُجِيرَنِي مِنَ ٱللَّهِ أَحَدࣱ وَلَنۡ أَجِدَ مِن دُونِهِۦ مُلۡتَحَدًا
72:22.en: Say: Lo! none can protect me from Allah, nor can I find any refuge beside Him

72:23.ar: إِلَّا بَلَٰغࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِسَٰلَٰتِهِۦۚ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدًا
72:23.en: (Mine is) but conveyance (of the Truth) from Allah, and His messages; and whoso disobeyeth Allah and His messenger, lo! his is fire of hell, wherein such dwell for ever

72:24.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا رَأَوۡاْ مَا يُوعَدُونَ فَسَيَعۡلَمُونَ مَنۡ أَضۡعَفُ نَاصِرࣰ ا وَأَقَلُّ عَدَدࣰ ا
72:24.en: Till (the day) when they shall behold that which they are promised (they may doubt); but then they will know (for certain) who is weaker in allies and less in multitude

72:25.ar: قُلۡ إِنۡ أَدۡرِيٓ أَقَرِيبࣱ مَّا تُوعَدُونَ أَمۡ يَجۡعَلُ لَهُۥ رَبِّيٓ أَمَدًا
72:25.en: Say (O Muhammad, unto the disbelievers): I know not whether that which ye are promised is nigh, or if my Lord hath set a distant term for it

72:26.ar: عَٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ فَلَا يُظۡهِرُ عَلَىٰ غَيۡبِهِۦٓ أَحَدًا
72:26.en: (He is) the Knower of the Unseen, and He revealeth unto none His secret

72:27.ar: إِلَّا مَنِ ٱرۡتَضَىٰ مِن رَّسُولࣲ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَسۡلُكُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ يَدَيۡهِ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِۦ رَصَدࣰ ا
72:27.en: Save unto every messenger whom He hath chosen, and then He maketh a guard to go before him and a guard behind him

72:28.ar: لِّيَعۡلَمَ أَن قَدۡ أَبۡلَغُواْ رِسَٰلَٰتِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَأَحَاطَ بِمَا لَدَيۡهِمۡ وَأَحۡصَىٰ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ عَدَدَۢا
72:28.en: That He may know that they have indeed conveyed the messages of their Lord. He surroundeth all their doings, and He keepeth count of all things

73:1.en: O thou wrapped up in thy raiment

73:2.en: Keep vigil the night long, save a little

73:3.en: A half thereof, or abate a little thereof

73:4.ar: أَوۡ زِدۡ عَلَيۡهِ وَرَتِّلِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ تَرۡتِيلًا
73:4.en: Or add (a little) thereto - and chant the Qur'an in measure

73:5.ar: إِنَّا سَنُلۡقِي عَلَيۡكَ قَوۡلࣰ ا ثَقِيلًا
73:5.en: For we shall charge thee with a word of weight

73:6.ar: إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ ٱلَّيۡلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطۡـࣰٔ ا وَأَقۡوَمُ قِيلًا
73:6.en: Lo! the vigil of the night is (a time) when impression is more keen and speech more certain

73:7.ar: إِنَّ لَكَ فِي ٱلنَّهَارِ سَبۡحࣰ ا طَوِيلࣰ ا
73:7.en: Lo! thou hast by day a chain of business

73:8.ar: وَٱذۡكُرِ ٱسۡمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلۡ إِلَيۡهِ تَبۡتِيلࣰ ا
73:8.en: So remember the name of thy Lord and devote thyself with a complete devotion

73:9.ar: رَّبُّ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَٱتَّخِذۡهُ وَكِيلࣰ ا
73:9.en: Lord of the East and the West; there is no Allah save Him; so choose thou Him alone for thy defender

73:10.ar: وَٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱهۡجُرۡهُمۡ هَجۡرࣰ ا جَمِيلࣰ ا
73:10.en: And bear with patience what they utter, and part from them with a fair leave-taking

73:11.ar: وَذَرۡنِي وَٱلۡمُكَذِّبِينَ أُوْلِي ٱلنَّعۡمَةِ وَمَهِّلۡهُمۡ قَلِيلًا
73:11.en: Leave Me to deal with the deniers, lords of ease and comfort (in this life); and do thou respite them awhile

73:12.ar: إِنَّ لَدَيۡنَآ أَنكَالࣰ ا وَجَحِيمࣰ ا
73:12.en: Lo! with Us are heavy fetters and a raging fire

73:13.ar: وَطَعَامࣰ ا ذَا غُصَّةࣲ وَعَذَابًا أَلِيمࣰ ا
73:13.en: And food which choketh (the partaker), and a painful doom

73:14.ar: يَوۡمَ تَرۡجُفُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَٱلۡجِبَالُ وَكَانَتِ ٱلۡجِبَالُ كَثِيبࣰ ا مَّهِيلًا
73:14.en: On the day when the earth and the hills rock, and the hills become a heap of running sand

73:15.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكُمۡ رَسُولࣰ ا شَٰهِدًا عَلَيۡكُمۡ كَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ رَسُولࣰ ا
73:15.en: Lo! We have sent unto you a messenger as witness against you, even as We sent unto Pharaoh a messenger

73:16.ar: فَعَصَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنُ ٱلرَّسُولَ فَأَخَذۡنَٰهُ أَخۡذࣰ ا وَبِيلࣰ ا
73:16.en: But Pharaoh rebelled against the messenger, whereupon We seized him with no gentle grip

73:17.ar: فَكَيۡفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِن كَفَرۡتُمۡ يَوۡمࣰ ا يَجۡعَلُ ٱلۡوِلۡدَٰنَ شِيبًا
73:17.en: Then how, if ye disbelieve, will ye protect yourselves upon the day which will turn children grey

73:18.ar: ٱلسَّمَآءُ مُنفَطِرُۢ بِهِۦۚ كَانَ وَعۡدُهُۥ مَفۡعُولًا
73:18.en: The very heaven being then rent asunder. His promise is to be fulfilled

73:19.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦ تَذۡكِرَةࣱۖ فَمَن شَآءَ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ سَبِيلًا
73:19.en: Lo! This is a Reminder. Let him who will, then, choose a way unto his Lord

73:20.ar: ۞إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعۡلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدۡنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَيِ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَنِصۡفَهُۥ وَثُلُثَهُۥ وَطَآئِفَةࣱ مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مَعَكَۚ وَٱللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَۚ عَلِمَ أَن لَّن تُحۡصُوهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡكُمۡۖ فَٱقۡرَءُواْ مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِۚ عَلِمَ أَن سَيَكُونُ مِنكُم مَّرۡضَىٰ وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضۡرِبُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَبۡتَغُونَ مِن فَضۡلِ ٱللَّهِ وَءَاخَرُونَ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَٱقۡرَءُواْ مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنۡهُۚ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَقۡرِضُواْ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنࣰ اۚ وَمَا تُقَدِّمُواْ لِأَنفُسِكُم مِّنۡ خَيۡرࣲ تَجِدُوهُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ خَيۡرࣰ ا وَأَعۡظَمَ أَجۡرࣰ اۚ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ ٱللَّهَۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمُۢ
73:20.en: Lo! thy Lord knoweth how thou keepest vigil sometimes nearly two-thirds of the night, or (sometimes) half or a third thereof, as do a party of those with thee. Allah measureth the night and the day. He knoweth that ye count it not, and turneth unto you in mercy. Recite, then, of the Qur'an that which is easy for you. He knoweth that there are sick folk among you, while others travel in the land in search of Allah's bounty, and others (still) are fighting for the cause of Allah. So recite of it that which is easy (for you), and establish worship and pay the poor-due, and (so) lend unto Allah a goodly loan. Whatsoever good ye send before you for your souls, ye will find it with Allah, better and greater in the recompense. And seek forgiveness of Allah. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

74:1.en: O thou enveloped in thy cloak

74:6.en: And show not favour, seeking wordly gain

74:7.en: For the sake of thy Lord, be patient

74:8.en: For when the trumpet shall sound

74:9.en: Surely that day will be a day of anguish

74:11.en: Leave Me (to deal) with him whom I created lonely

74:12.ar: وَجَعَلۡتُ لَهُۥ مَالࣰ ا مَّمۡدُودࣰ ا
74:12.en: And then bestowed upon him ample means

74:13.en: And sons abiding in his presence

74:15.en: Yet he desireth that I should give more

74:16.ar: كَلَّآۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لِأٓيَٰتِنَا عَنِيدࣰ ا
74:16.en: Nay! For lo! he hath been stubborn to Our revelations

74:17.en: On him I shall impose a fearful doom

74:18.en: For lo! he did consider; then he planned

74:20.en: Again (self-)destroyed is he, how he planned

74:22.en: Then frowned he and showed displeasure

74:23.en: Then turned he away in pride

74:24.ar: فَقَالَ إِنۡ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحۡرࣱ يُؤۡثَرُ
74:24.en: And said: This is naught else than magic from of old

74:25.en: This is naught else than speech of mortal man

74:26.en: Him shall I fling unto the burning

74:27.en: Ah, what will convey unto thee what that burning is

74:28.en: It leaveth naught; it spareth naught

74:31.ar: وَمَا جَعَلۡنَآ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلنَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَٰٓئِكَةࣰۖ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا عِدَّتَهُمۡ إِلَّا فِتۡنَةࣰ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِيَسۡتَيۡقِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَيَزۡدَادَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِيمَٰنࣰ ا وَلَا يَرۡتَابَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَلِيَقُولَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضࣱ وَٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلࣰ اۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَۚ وَمَا هِيَ إِلَّا ذِكۡرَىٰ لِلۡبَشَرِ
74:31.en: We have appointed only angels to be wardens of the Fire, and their number have We made to be a stumbling-block for those who disbelieve; that those to whom the Scripture hath been given may have certainty, and that believers may increase in faith; and that those to whom the Scripture hath been given and believers may not doubt; and that those in whose hearts there is disease, and disbelievers, may say: What meaneth Allah by this similitude? Thus Allah sendeth astray whom He will, and whom He will He guideth. None knoweth the hosts of thy Lord save Him. This is naught else than a Reminder unto mortals

74:33.en: And the night when it withdraweth

74:34.en: And the dawn when it shineth forth

74:35.en: Lo! this is one of the greatest (portents)

74:37.ar: لِمَن شَآءَ مِنكُمۡ أَن يَتَقَدَّمَ أَوۡ يَتَأَخَّرَ
74:37.en: Unto him of you who will advance or hang back

74:38.en: Every soul is a pledge for its own deeds

74:39.en: Save those who will stand on the right hand

74:40.en: In gardens they will ask one another

74:42.en: What hath brought you to this burning

74:43.en: They will answer: We were not of those who prayed

74:44.en: Nor did we feed the wretched

74:45.en: We used to wade (in vain dispute) with (all) waders

74:46.en: And we used to deny the Day of Judgment

74:47.en: Till the Inevitable came unto us

74:48.en: The mediation of no mediators will avail them then

74:49.en: Why now turn they away from the Admonishment

74:52.ar: بَلۡ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ ٱمۡرِيࣲٕ مِّنۡهُمۡ أَن يُؤۡتَىٰ صُحُفࣰ ا مُّنَشَّرَةࣰ‏
74:52.en: Nay, but everyone of them desireth that he should be given open pages (from Allah)

74:53.en: Nay, verily. They fear not the Hereafter

74:54.en: Nay, verily. Lo! this is an Admonishment

74:56.ar: وَمَا يَذۡكُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُۚ هُوَ أَهۡلُ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ وَأَهۡلُ ٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِ
74:56.en: And they will not heed unless Allah willeth (it). He is the fount of fear. He is the fount of Mercy

75:1.en: Nay, I swear by the Day of Resurrection

75:2.en: Nay, I swear by the accusing soul (that this Scripture is true)

75:3.en: Thinketh man that We shall not assemble his bones

75:4.ar: بَلَىٰ قَٰدِرِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُۥ
75:4.en: Yea, verily. We are Able to restore his very fingers

75:5.en: But man would fain deny what is before him

75:6.en: He asketh: When will be this Day of Resurrection

75:9.en: And sun and moon are united

75:10.en: On that day man will cry: Whither to flee

75:12.en: Unto thy Lord is the recourse that day

75:13.ar: يُنَبَّؤُاْ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بِمَا قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ
75:13.en: On that day man is told the tale of that which he hath sent before and left behind

75:14.en: Oh, but man is a telling witness against himself

75:16.ar: لَا تُحَرِّكۡ بِهِۦ لِسَانَكَ لِتَعۡجَلَ بِهِۦٓ
75:16.en: Stir not thy tongue herewith to hasten it

75:17.en: Lo! upon Us (resteth) the putting together thereof and the reading thereof

75:18.en: And when We read it, follow thou the reading

75:19.en: Then lo! upon Us (resteth) the explanation thereof

75:20.en: Nay, but ye do love the fleeting Now

75:22.en: That day will faces be resplendent

75:24.en: And that day will other faces be despondent

75:25.en: Thou wilt know that some great disaster is about to fall on them

75:26.en: Nay, but when the life cometh up to the throat

75:27.en: And men say: Where is the wizard (who can save him now)

75:28.en: And he knoweth that it is the parting

75:29.en: And agony is heaped on agony

75:30.en: Unto thy Lord that day will be the driving

75:31.en: For he neither trusted, nor prayed

75:33.en: Then went he to his folk with glee

75:35.en: Again nearer unto thee and nearer (is the doom)

75:36.en: Thinketh man that he is to be left aimless

75:37.ar: أَلَمۡ يَكُ نُطۡفَةࣰ مِّن مَّنِيࣲّ يُمۡنَىٰ
75:37.en: Was he not a drop of fluid which gushed forth

75:38.en: Then he became a clot; then (Allah) shaped and fashioned

75:39.en: And made of him a pair, the male and female

75:40.ar: أَلَيۡسَ ذَٰلِكَ بِقَٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يُحۡـِۧيَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ
75:40.en: Is not He (Who doeth so) Able to bring the dead to life

0Tw2cxEhI2w.speaker: adnan
0Tw2cxEhI2w.speaker_note: his A Juz A Day series; welcomes viewers and teaches throughout in his own voice
0Tw2cxEhI2w.title: A Juz A Day: 29th Juz - The Hereafter is Imminent
0Tw2cxEhI2w.one_line: Al-Mulk through Al-Qiyamah: the Hereafter is closer than we think, and inviting others to Allah is a shared duty that needs patience and night prayer.
0Tw2cxEhI2w.summary: He names two threads running through the 29th juz: the Hereafter is imminent, and inviting people to Islam is a binding responsibility that every believer now shares with the Prophet. Al-Mulk shows a flawless creation designed to decline so we remember the Judgment, tests us by the quality rather than the quantity of deeds, and makes clear that everyone in the fire received the message and rejected it. It also models dawah that appeals to reason and to the heart. Al-Qalam repeatedly tells the Prophet to be patient, play the long game, and not compromise on fundamentals, with the greedy owners of the garden and Yunus as warnings. Al-Haqqah and Al-Maarij paint the records given in the right and left hands, and he notes that failing to encourage feeding the poor is listed beside disbelief. Consistent prayer, he argues, brings consistency to life so believers are not thrown by good or bad. Nuh's own account of his dawah, the jinn who listened unseen, and the commands of Al-Muzzammil and Al-Muddaththir teach that spiritual connection through night prayer must come before preaching, that you step out of your comfort zone, and that you do your part while Allah handles the results.

outline.heading: Opening
Two themes: the Hereafter is imminent and dawah is our duty
outline.gist: Eleven mostly Makkan surahs; the Prophet carried the duty of inviting to Islam best, and after him it falls on all of us.

outline.heading: The virtue of Al-Mulk
outline.gist: The Prophet taught it be recited before sleep; it protects from the punishment of the grave and intercedes on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: A flawless creation, with decline by design
outline.gist: Look again and again and you find no flaw; ageing and decline are intended so we realize creation will end and we will be held to account.

outline.heading: Best in deeds, not most in deeds
outline.gist: Allah created life and death to test who is best in deeds: quality matters more than quantity.

outline.heading: Did no warner come to you?
outline.gist: Hell roars and boils over, and every group thrown in admits a warner came and they called him a liar; had they listened and reasoned they would not be there.

outline.heading: No one enters hell without receiving the message
outline.gist: Polytheist, agnostic or atheist, those in the fire all rejected the message; those it never reached will be tested on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: He knows what is in the hearts
outline.gist: Those in awe of their unseen Lord are forgiven; how could the Creator not know His creation? A verse worth keeping in front of you.

outline.heading: The smoothed earth and the birds held aloft
outline.gist: The earth is made easy for us to live on but is not forever; only the Most Compassionate holds the birds in the sky.

outline.heading: Dawah to the mind: who provides if He withholds?
outline.gist: When Allah puts something out of reach no one can bring it, as the pandemic showed; when He gives, no one can stop it.

outline.heading: Dawah to the heart: hearing, sight and intellect
outline.gist: Allah appeals to our faculties and gratitude, then warns of the faces that darken when the torment draws near.

outline.heading: If your water sank into the earth
outline.gist: Our power is fractional and on loan from Allah, which is why we submit to Him and invite others to do so.

outline.heading: Al-Qalam: be patient and play the long game
outline.gist: A recurring Quranic message to the Prophet and to us: do not give up on people or on our own struggles.

outline.heading: By the Pen: destined to be the final prophet
outline.gist: The Pen wrote all destiny before creation; the Prophet's role and his outstanding character were written and cannot be taken from him.

outline.heading: No compromise on the fundamentals
outline.gist: The Prophet compromised on terms at Hudaybiyyah for peace, but never on the principles of the deen.

outline.heading: The owners of the garden
outline.gist: They swore to harvest everything without saying in sha Allah and to keep the poor out, then found their garden burnt to ashes.

outline.heading: How a believer responds to loss
outline.gist: Unlike their panic and mutual blame, a believer says alhamdulillah whether given or denied, knowing it is decreed.

outline.heading: What is the basis of your morality?
outline.gist: Quraysh are asked whether they have a scripture or a binding promise from Allah that guarantees them whatever they choose.

outline.heading: The day the shin is bared
outline.gist: Those who refused to prostrate when able will be unable to on that day, separating believers from rejecters; he affirms the attribute without asking how.

outline.heading: Do not be like the man of the whale
outline.gist: Yunus left his people before permission; the Prophet is told not to give up on his, since a happy ending is possible.

outline.heading: Al-Haqqah: the inevitable hour, and Thamud and Ad
outline.gist: The surah names the event and asks what will make you comprehend it, then recounts the blast and the seven-night wind.

outline.heading: Pharaoh, Lut's cities and the ark of Nuh
outline.gist: The history lesson is for attentive ears: the punishment that wiped out earlier nations can fall on anyone, and the hereafter is worse.

outline.heading: The trumpet, the crushed earth and the throne
outline.gist: Earth and mountains are flattened, the sky is torn, and eight angels bear the throne as all secrets are exposed.

outline.heading: Here, read my record: the right hand
outline.gist: The joyful believer knew he would face his reckoning and now enjoys a lofty garden with fruit within reach.

outline.heading: The left hand: seize him, he did not urge feeding the poor
outline.gist: He wishes death had been the end; a group of angels shackles him because he had no faith and did not encourage feeding the poor.

outline.heading: Not a poet or fortune teller; if he had fabricated
outline.gist: The hypothetical that the Prophet would be seized if he invented anything shows his accountability is the highest, though it never happened.

outline.heading: The absolute truth: glorify your Lord
outline.gist: The surah ends where it began, with the truth, and so we glorify Allah the Most Great.

outline.heading: Al-Maarij: the challenger who demanded punishment
outline.gist: The punishment will not be averted; it comes from the Lord of the ascending ways on a day that feels fifty thousand years long.

outline.heading: Beautiful patience
outline.gist: Ignore those trying to provoke; they see the day as far, believers see it as inevitable.

outline.heading: Friendships removed: ransoming one's family
outline.gist: The criminal would hand over spouse, children, siblings and clan to save himself, but faces a flame that strips the scalp.

outline.heading: Humans created anxious
outline.gist: People panic when hit by evil and hoard when touched by good.

outline.heading: Consistent prayer brings a consistent life
outline.gist: Those steady in their salah stay calm in good and bad times instead of swinging between highs and lows.

outline.heading: The rest of the believers' traits
outline.gist: A known share for the poor, fear of their Lord, chastity, keeping trusts, and the courage to give honest testimony; faith brings out the best of human nature.

outline.heading: Nuh tells his own story: fingers in their ears
outline.gist: Told from Nuh's point of view, he called them day and night and they stuffed their ears and covered their faces, ruder than someone on their phone.

outline.heading: Seek forgiveness and receive rain, wealth and children
outline.gist: Nuh appealed to reason and emotion: forgiveness brings worldly good too, and the Creator who made you in stages and grows you like plants will bring you back.

outline.heading: Even Nuh had a limit
outline.gist: After long patience he prayed against them and they were wiped out; the Prophet is told not to give up on his people yet.

outline.heading: Al-Jinn: listeners you never knew about
outline.gist: A group of jinn heard the Quran, believed and returned to their people; the repeated formula ties the whole surah to what was revealed about them.

outline.heading: Do your job and Allah takes care of the results
outline.gist: The Prophet did not know the jinn heard his Fajr recitation and set off a chain of conversions, so never lose hope.

outline.heading: They crowded to hear; I only convey
outline.gist: The jinn nearly tripped over each other listening; the Prophet declares he has no power to harm or benefit and does not know when the promise comes.

outline.heading: Al-Muzzammil: you wrapped in your cloak, stand at night
outline.gist: After the first revelation the Prophet asked to be covered; he is now told to pray much of the night and recite slowly before a heavy word is sent.

outline.heading: Spirituality before preaching
outline.gist: Night prayer makes the deepest impression; that connection gives the strength to endure insults, ignore them graciously and play the long game.

outline.heading: A day that turns children's hair grey
outline.gist: As Pharaoh was punished for disobeying his messenger, how will deniers protect themselves on such a day?

outline.heading: Recite what is easy and lend Allah a good loan
outline.gist: Allowance is made for tiredness, travel and battle, but keep the night prayer, pay zakat and give, as Allah repays and multiplies it.

outline.heading: Al-Muddaththir: arise and warn
outline.gist: Break out of your shell and comfort zone to give dawah, keep pure, and do not do a favour expecting more in return.

outline.heading: The chief of Quraysh who contemplated
outline.gist: A powerful, wealthy leader thought hard, frowned and finally called the Quran ancient magic, the words of a man.

outline.heading: Manufacturing a label to dismiss the Quran
outline.gist: He knew it was the truth but would not give up his seat of power; his talking points became Quraysh's, and his acceptance could have brought most of them.

outline.heading: Every soul is hostage to what it earned
outline.gist: Choices have consequences; only the people of the right are free because their deeds were good.

outline.heading: What landed you in hell? No prayer, no feeding the poor
outline.gist: Feeding the poor appears again as the second reason, after not praying, along with indulging in falsehood and denying the Judgment.

outline.heading: A reminder for whoever wills
outline.gist: A person must seek guidance and Allah gives it; He alone is worthy to be feared and to forgive.

outline.heading: Al-Qiyamah: restoring even the fingertips
outline.gist: Allah can reassemble bones down to the fingertips that uniquely identify each person; the sun and moon will be joined.

outline.heading: No escape: the soul testifies against itself
outline.gist: Each person is told what he sent forth and left behind, and his own self bears witness.

outline.heading: Do not rush your tongue with the Quran
outline.gist: A tangent reassuring the Prophet he will retain the revelation, teaching him how to learn as well as what to learn.

outline.heading: Left without purpose?
outline.gist: The One who made us from a drop and shaped male and female can bring the dead back, so life has a purpose: worship.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Everyone in hell received the message and rejected it; Allah will test those it never reached.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Records in the right and left hands, and the abandonment of family and friends on that day.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: Al-Mulk models dawah that addresses both reason and the heart.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: Nuh's patient invitation and the unseen jinn show that you do your part and Allah handles the results.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam

themes.label: Patience (sabr) and perseverance

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance

themes.note: The garden owners' greed and assumed security, and the believer's alhamdulillah whether given or denied.
