themes.note: Humans are not left without purpose; the One who created can resurrect.

hadith.gist: Recite Surah Al-Mulk before sleeping; it protects from the punishment of the grave and will intercede for its reader on the Day of Judgment.
After the first revelation the Prophet returned and asked to be covered so he could calm down.

maxims: Quality of deeds matters more than quantity
Play the long game; don't give up on people
No one goes to hell without the message
Consistent prayer brings a consistent life
Spirituality before preaching
Do your job and Allah takes care of the results

stories.who: The owners of the garden
stories.point: Greed and forgetting Allah's will cost them the harvest; a believer accepts loss with praise.

stories.who: Yunus, the man of the whale
stories.point: Leaving one's people before permission is a mistake; there can still be a happy ending, so do not give up.

stories.who: Nuh and his people
stories.point: Patient, gentle and logical dawah over centuries met with contempt, until even Nuh reached his limit.

stories.who: The jinn who heard the Quran
stories.point: Your words can transform people you never knew were listening.

stories.who: Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah
stories.point: He knew the Quran was true but fabricated the label of magic to protect his power.

contemporary: The COVID-19 pandemic as an example of something Allah put out of reach despite everyone's efforts
Talking to someone who is on their phone as a picture of rudeness
takeaways: Recite Al-Mulk before sleeping
Aim for the best deeds rather than the most deeds
Keep inviting people with patience and never compromise on the fundamentals
Build your connection with Allah through night prayer before trying to preach
Feed the poor and encourage others to do so

45:14.ar: قُل لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يَغۡفِرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ لَا يَرۡجُونَ أَيَّامَ ٱللَّهِ لِيَجۡزِيَ قَوۡمَۢا بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ
45:14.en: Tell those who believe to forgive those who hope not for the days of Allah; in order that He may requite folk what they used to earn

43:88.ar: وَقِيلِهِۦ يَٰرَبِّ إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ قَوۡمࣱ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
43:88.en: And he saith: O my Lord! Lo! these are a folk who believe not

43:89.ar: فَٱصۡفَحۡ عَنۡهُمۡ وَقُلۡ سَلَٰمࣱۚ فَسَوۡفَ يَعۡلَمُونَ
43:89.en: Then bear with them (O Muhammad) and say: Peace. But they will come to know

24:22.ar: وَلَا يَأۡتَلِ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡفَضۡلِ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلسَّعَةِ أَن يُؤۡتُوٓاْ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَلۡيَعۡفُواْ وَلۡيَصۡفَحُوٓاْۗ أَلَا تُحِبُّونَ أَن يَغۡفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
24:22.en: And let not those who possess dignity and ease among you swear not to give to the near of kin and to the needy, and to fugitives for the cause of Allah. Let them forgive and show indulgence. Yearn ye not that Allah may forgive you? Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

42:43.ar: وَلَمَن صَبَرَ وَغَفَرَ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَمِنۡ عَزۡمِ ٱلۡأُمُورِ
42:43.en: And verily whoso is patient and forgiveth - lo! that, verily, is (of) the steadfast heart of things

14:35.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمُ رَبِّ ٱجۡعَلۡ هَٰذَا ٱلۡبَلَدَ ءَامِنࣰ ا وَٱجۡنُبۡنِي وَبَنِيَّ أَن نَّعۡبُدَ ٱلۡأَصۡنَامَ
14:35.en: And when Abraham said: My Lord! Make safe this territory, and preserve me and my sons from serving idols

14:36.ar: رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضۡلَلۡنَ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِۖ فَمَن تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُۥ مِنِّيۖ وَمَنۡ عَصَانِي فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
14:36.en: My Lord! Lo! they have led many of mankind astray. But whoso followeth me, he verily is of me. And whoso disobeyeth me - Still Thou art Forgiving, Merciful

5:118.ar: إِن تُعَذِّبۡهُمۡ فَإِنَّهُمۡ عِبَادُكَۖ وَإِن تَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ فَإِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
5:118.en: If Thou punish them, lo! they are Thy slaves, and if Thou forgive them (lo! they are Thy slaves). Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Mighty, the Wise

59:10.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا ٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَلِإِخۡوَٰنِنَا ٱلَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِٱلۡإِيمَٰنِ وَلَا تَجۡعَلۡ فِي قُلُوبِنَا غِلࣰّ ا لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ رَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
59:10.en: And those who came (into the faith) after them say: Our Lord! Forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith, and place not in our hearts any rancour toward those who believe. Our Lord! Thou art Full of Pity, Merciful

ZA7FIIfzn24.title: The Values of Islam: Forgiveness and Pardoning (Maghfirah and 'Afw)
ZA7FIIfzn24.one_line: Forgiveness and pardoning are high ideals built on justice; on the 27th night, forgive others as you hope Allah forgives you.
ZA7FIIfzn24.summary: On the eve of the 27th night of Ramadan he turns to forgiveness and pardoning as they come from people, not from Allah. These are high-order ideals that the earlier ethics exist to protect: one cannot preach forgiveness where rights are violated, just as outward sunnah means nothing alongside eating haram. He lists the scholars' conditions for forgiveness: it must be for Allah, the wronged person must be capable of reclaiming the right, and it must lead to reconciliation rather than encouraging the wrongdoer. Asking the oppressed to forgive while their right is still held is shameful; forgiving what you cannot reclaim is weakness. Forgiveness means not seeking accountability and unloading a burden the wrongdoer has long forgotten, though distance may remain; pardoning goes further, restoring the relationship as if nothing happened. He tells of Abu Bakr resuming support of Mistah after the slander of Aishah when the Quran asked whether he did not love Allah's forgiveness, admitting he has not yet managed such forgiveness. He cites Ibrahim and Isa leaving their people to Allah's forgiveness, the Prophet's night spent on one verse, and the dua against grudges. He asks each listener to find someone to forgive tonight, stressing the choice is theirs.

outline.heading: Opening
Forgiving others on the 27th night
outline.gist: To obtain forgiveness on this night one must offer it to others; the talk concerns forgiveness from people, not from Allah.

outline.heading: Ideals that the basic ethics protect
outline.gist: Forgiveness and pardoning are high ideals of elegance that require justice and trustworthiness first; the series was ordered for this reason.

outline.heading: Ideals without foundations
outline.gist: Outward sunnah alongside haram earnings makes no sense; justice must be bolted down before calling the oppressed to forgive.

outline.heading: Condition of forgiveness: for the sake of Allah
outline.gist: Forgiveness is not a transaction or a favour to be returned later.

outline.heading: Condition of forgiveness: capability
outline.gist: One can only forgive a right one is able to reclaim; telling the oppressed to forgive while their right is still taken is shameful.

outline.heading: Condition of forgiveness: no harm
outline.gist: Forgive only when it brings reconciliation, not when it encourages the wrongdoer to keep transgressing.

outline.heading: Reclaim the right first
outline.gist: The Prophet told the companions to go after the wealth taken from them before choosing to forgive, since forgiving what you cannot reach is weakness.

outline.heading: Forgive those who do not hope for Allah's days
outline.gist: The Quran urges forgiving offenders because their reckoning is heavy; forgiveness goes against human nature and takes deliberate effort.

outline.heading: Forgiveness unloads your own burden
outline.gist: The wrongdoer forgets while the wronged carries the bitterness; forgiving cleanses the heart, though trust and distance may remain.

outline.heading: Pardoning restores the glass
outline.gist: 'Afw goes beyond forgiveness, returning the relationship to how it was, as the Prophet was told to pardon and say peace.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr, Aishah and Mistah
outline.gist: The slander devastated Abu Bakr, who swore to cut off support from Mistah, a relative he had been funding.

outline.heading: Do you not love that Allah forgives you?
outline.gist: The verse revealed after the slander moved Abu Bakr to restore Mistah's support for life.

outline.heading: Maybe tonight
outline.gist: He admits he has never managed to imagine forgiving like Abu Bakr and hopes each year this night will be the one.

outline.heading: Forgiveness is true strength and raises rank
outline.gist: Those who persevere and forgive show real resolve, and Allah only increases a servant in honour for pardoning.

outline.heading: Ibrahim and Isa leave their people to Allah
outline.gist: Both prophets entrusted sinners to Allah's forgiveness, and the Prophet spent a whole night reciting Isa's verse.

outline.heading: The Prophet carried no grudges
outline.gist: Pardoning differs from mercy, which is empathy, and from tawbah, which is changing oneself.

outline.heading: A dua against grudges
outline.gist: Later believers asked Allah to forgive those before them and remove any grudge from their hearts.

outline.heading: Most grievances are petty: let them go
outline.gist: Usually you could reclaim your right but it is not worth it, and living with the bitterness wastes your life; still, no one can force you to forgive.

outline.heading: Who do you need to forgive?
outline.gist: He asks each listener to find someone to forgive, especially those who never apologized, promising Allah will give more in return.

outline.heading: Allah loves to pardon
outline.gist: The Prophet's dua for these nights asks the One who loves pardoning; the question is whether we can do it ourselves.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Forgiveness and pardoning are ideals with conditions, an unburdening of the self and a way to earn Allah's pardon.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Rights must be restored before the oppressed are asked to forgive; forgiving what you cannot reclaim is weakness.

themes.label: Values, principles and ethics as a system
themes.note: High ideals sit on the shoulders of baseline ethics and cannot exist without them.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: The 27th night is a time to seek Allah's pardon by pardoning others.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: Abu Bakr's forgiveness of Mistah after the slander of his daughter.

themes.label: Envy, anger and other diseases of the heart
themes.note: Carrying grudges only burdens oneself; believers ask Allah to cleanse their hearts of them.

quran.point: Tell the believers to forgive those who do not hope for the days of Allah
These people will not believe; pardon them and say peace
Let the people of means not swear off giving to relatives; let them pardon and overlook; do you not love that Allah forgives you
Whoever is patient and forgives, that is of true resolve
Ibrahim leaves those who disobey him to Allah's forgiveness and mercy
Isa: if You punish them they are Your servants, and if You forgive them You are the Mighty, the Wise
Dua to forgive earlier believers and remove grudges from the heart

hadith.gist: Allah does not increase a servant who pardons except in honour
The Prophet stood a whole night repeating one verse, Isa's words about forgiving his people
O Allah, You are the Pardoner and You love to pardon, so pardon me

maxims: Forgiving what you cannot reclaim is weakness, not forgiveness
These are values of elegance, built on the basics
Forgiveness unburdens you; the wrongdoer already forgot
Pardoning puts the broken glass back together
Maybe tonight

stories.who: Abu Bakr and Mistah
stories.point: Despite Mistah's role in slandering Aishah, Abu Bakr resumed his support because he wanted Allah's forgiveness.

stories.who: Companions whose wealth was seized in Makkah
stories.point: The Prophet told them to reclaim their rights first and then decide whether to forgive.

stories.who: The Prophet's night with Isa's verse
stories.point: He learned to be a forgiving soul and wept over a verse entrusting sinners to Allah's forgiveness.

takeaways: Identify someone you have not forgiven and work on forgiving them on this night
Do not pressure the oppressed to forgive while their rights are still taken
Forgive for Allah's sake, and only where it brings reconciliation
Let go of petty grievances rather than living with bitterness
Ask Allah to remove grudges from your heart

QfqJzQzsuNM.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 28 - Quranic Themes: Insights
QfqJzQzsuNM.one_line: Insight as seeing past appearances: man is a witness against himself (75:14-15), every soul knows what it brought (81:14), and bystanders are not innocent (85:7).
QfqJzQzsuNM.summary: He defines insight as seeing what lies beneath surfaces and argues that losing it means losing everything. In an age of cosmetic surgery and AI fakes the eyes are easily fooled, but the heart is not: gut feelings are not proof, yet should never be ignored, and many great scholars were blind yet saw deeply. Insight is strong in youth and either sharpens or dulls with age; without it people choose ruinous spouses or, worst of all, arrive on Judgement Day sure they did well, the greatest losers of 18:103-104. From al-Qiyamah he shows that doubts about resurrection mask a wish to follow desire, while 75:14-15 says every person is a witness to himself despite his excuses. We can fool everyone, even ourselves for a while, but not Allah, just as parents see through a child's lies. At-Takwir's scenes of cosmic collapse end with every soul knowing what it has brought, so he urges people to level with themselves now and ask for mercy like Yusuf's brothers with their poor goods, since no one else really cares. Finally al-Buruj's people of the ditch include those who sat and watched: silence before oppression is a choice that will be answered for.

outline.heading: Sight versus insight
outline.gist: Eyes see packaging and masks; insight sees what is inside and what really happened.

outline.heading: Lose insight and you lose everything
outline.gist: Eyes are fooled by any magician, but looking with the eyes of the heart always finds the way back to what is right.

outline.heading: An age of optical illusions
outline.gist: Cosmetic surgery remakes people and AI will make every photo and video worthless as evidence until verified, yet the heart still senses when something is wrong.

outline.heading: Do not ignore your gut
outline.gist: Intuition is not proof and should not be acted on alone, but it is given for a reason and should be heard and honed.

outline.heading: Blind scholars and blind hearts
outline.gist: Countless scholars were born blind yet had extraordinary insight into revelation and the seerah; it is hearts that go blind, not eyes.

outline.heading: Healthy bodies without insight
outline.gist: Some people lecture on morality with no insight into the state of their own lives and families.

outline.heading: Insight and choosing a spouse
outline.gist: The young see clearly, but insight sharpens or dulls with age; a woman blind to a harmful man or a man losing his family over a bad match shows desire overriding insight.

outline.heading: 18:103-104: the greatest losers
outline.gist: Self-honesty keeps you from drifting unaware; the biggest losers are those who thought they were doing well and arrive expecting approval.

outline.heading: His friend who always aced the exam
outline.gist: A friend left every exam certain he had done well and scored half; over-optimism without honest self-assessment costs dearly.

outline.heading: 75:3-12: the real reason for denial
outline.gist: Man claims Allah cannot reassemble his bones, but the real issue is wanting an excuse to follow desire guilt-free; on that day he will ask where to flee.

outline.heading: 75:14-15: a witness against himself
outline.gist: Whatever excuses he offers, man knows exactly why he did what he did; he can fool spouse, parents and community, even himself, but not Allah.

outline.heading: An inner compass
outline.gist: Imagine not knowing your own motives; Allah gave a compass that always tells you whether you were selfish, petty or sincere.

outline.heading: Admit it to yourself
outline.gist: 75:13 says man will be told all he did, though he does not need telling; you need not confess to others, but you must be honest with yourself.

outline.heading: Children's lies and our excuses to Allah
outline.gist: Parents see straight through a child's lies, and we do the same with Allah; raising children is the closest thing we have to understanding that relationship.

outline.heading: 81:1-4: the cosmos unravels
outline.gist: The sun wound into a ball, stars falling to dust, mountains moved like powder and pregnant animals abandoned.

outline.heading: 81:5: the animals gathered
outline.gist: Every creature is a nation like us and will be brought back, so treat animals as neighbours and partners on earth.

outline.heading: 81:6-7: seas ablaze and souls paired
outline.gist: Oceans catch fire, and each person is joined with those most like them; no one stands alone.

outline.heading: 81:8-11: the buried girl is asked
outline.gist: Murdered children will be asked for what sin they were killed, including babies buried under their bombed homes; records are spread and the sky stripped away.

outline.heading: 81:12-14: every soul knows what it brought
outline.gist: Hell is kindled and Paradise brought near, and every soul knows exactly what it carries.

outline.heading: Level with yourself now
outline.gist: Use the insight you already have to admit who you are without decoration; that honesty is the launching pad for change.

outline.heading: A dua that relies on mercy alone
outline.gist: In the last nights, ask Allah as Yusuf's brothers asked with their worthless goods: we bring little, so be charitable to us.

outline.heading: No one else really cares
outline.gist: The social web of opinions and status means nothing; people will not ask after you, and the only one who has ever truly cared is Allah.

outline.heading: Standing amid it all, knowing
outline.gist: As creation is remade you will know what you brought; leveling with yourself now spares you the greatest disappointment.

outline.heading: Interlude
The people of the ditch
outline.gist: A king burned believers one by one in a fiery trench for refusing to give up their faith, and they stood firm.

outline.heading: Oaths by the witness and the witnessed
outline.gist: Allah swears by the constellations, the promised day and every witness and thing witnessed before cursing the people of the ditch.

outline.heading: Three groups at the trench
outline.gist: The cursed are not only those who dug it; there were the believers, the criminals and a third group who sat and watched.

outline.heading: The silent majority
outline.gist: The neutral onlookers who see and have opinions but say nothing let a harmful minority set the norm; he calls them the biggest evil.

outline.heading: Doing nothing is a choice
outline.gist: The idea that it is not your problem is foreign to Islam; standing by while people are stripped of rights is a decision.

outline.heading: The eldest who 'didn't do anything'
outline.gist: Parents blame the eldest when the younger ones wreck the house; before Allah, having done nothing is exactly the charge.

outline.heading: Witnesses will answer
outline.gist: Those who watched oppression and went to sleep knew what they could have done; you would never accept that excuse if you were the one under fire.

themes.label: Insight (basirah), intuition and seeing past appearances
themes.note: Insight sees beneath surfaces; losing it means losing everything, so intuition must be heard and strengthened.

themes.label: Technology, AI, social media and attention
themes.note: AI fakes and cosmetic surgery mean the eyes can no longer be trusted.

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: Choosing a spouse driven by desire without insight leads to years of harm.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Man is a witness to himself; he must admit his reality to himself rather than repeat his own lies until he believes them.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: Excuses do not work before Allah, who knows motives as a parent sees through a child's lie.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: At-Takwir's scenes of collapse end with every soul knowing what it has brought.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: Babies killed under their bombed homes will be asked, like the buried girl, for what sin they died.

themes.label: Hope, fear and the balance between them
themes.note: Admit you have nothing to show and rely entirely on Allah's mercy, like Yusuf's brothers.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: The bystanders at the trench share the guilt; silence in the face of oppression is a choice.

quran.point: It is not the eyes that go blind but the hearts within the chests.
The greatest losers in deeds are those who thought they were doing well.
Every creature forms a community like ours, so animals deserve respect.
Yusuf's brothers bring goods of little value and ask him to be charitable; a model for asking Allah's mercy.

maxims: When you lose insight, you lose everything
Look with the eyes of your heart, not your skull
Don't act on your gut, but don't ignore it
Level with yourself
The biggest evil is the silent majority
Not doing anything is also a choice

stories.who: Scholars who were born blind
stories.point: Their insight into revelation was extraordinary; hearts, not eyes, go blind.

stories.who: His university friend and exams
stories.point: Always sure he had done well and always wrong; misplaced optimism reflects a lack of insight.

stories.who: Children lying to their parents
stories.point: Parents see through it at once; our excuses to Allah are just as transparent.

stories.who: The brothers of Yusuf
stories.point: They admitted their goods were poor and asked for charity; ask Allah the same way.

stories.who: The people of the ditch
stories.point: Believers burned for their faith; the curse falls also on those who sat and watched.

stories.who: The eldest child who did nothing
stories.point: Standing by while harm happens is itself the failure being judged.

contemporary: AI-generated images and video making photographic evidence unreliable in courts
Cosmetic surgery remaking appearances
Children killed under the rubble of bombed homes
The silent majority watching oppression and saying nothing
takeaways: Listen to your gut feelings without treating them as proof, and work to strengthen your insight.
Admit to yourself honestly what you do and why, without the excuses you give others.
Ask Allah for mercy on the basis of His generosity, not your deeds.
Stop seeking the approval of people who will soon forget you, and bring Allah something worth showing.
Speak up and act against oppression you witness; staying silent is a choice you will answer for.

60:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءَ تُلۡقُونَ إِلَيۡهِم بِٱلۡمَوَدَّةِ وَقَدۡ كَفَرُواْ بِمَا جَآءَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ يُخۡرِجُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ وَإِيَّاكُمۡ أَن تُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ رَبِّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ خَرَجۡتُمۡ جِهَٰدࣰ ا فِي سَبِيلِي وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ مَرۡضَاتِيۚ تُسِرُّونَ إِلَيۡهِم بِٱلۡمَوَدَّةِ وَأَنَا۠ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَآ أَخۡفَيۡتُمۡ وَمَآ أَعۡلَنتُمۡۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡهُ مِنكُمۡ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
60:1.en: O ye who believe! Choose not My enemy and your enemy for allies. Do ye give them friendship when they disbelieve in that truth which hath come unto you, driving out the messenger and you because ye believe in Allah, your Lord? If ye have come forth to strive in My way and seeking My good pleasure, (show them not friendship). Do ye show friendship unto them in secret, when I am Best Aware of what ye hide and what ye proclaim? And whosoever doeth it among you, he verily hath strayed from the right way

60:7.ar: ۞عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَجۡعَلَ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَبَيۡنَ ٱلَّذِينَ عَادَيۡتُم مِّنۡهُم مَّوَدَّةࣰۚ وَٱللَّهُ قَدِيرࣱۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
60:7.en: It may be that Allah will ordain love between you and those of them with whom ye are at enmity. Allah is Mighty, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

60:8.ar: لَّا يَنۡهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يُقَٰتِلُوكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَلَمۡ يُخۡرِجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ أَن تَبَرُّوهُمۡ وَتُقۡسِطُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُقۡسِطِينَ
60:8.en: Allah forbiddeth you not those who warred not against you on account of religion and drove you not out from your homes, that ye should show them kindness and deal justly with them. Lo! Allah loveth the just dealers

60:9.ar: إِنَّمَا يَنۡهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ قَٰتَلُوكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَأَخۡرَجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ وَظَٰهَرُواْ عَلَىٰٓ إِخۡرَاجِكُمۡ أَن تَوَلَّوۡهُمۡۚ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّهُمۡ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
60:9.en: Allah forbiddeth you only those who warred against you on account of religion and have driven you out from your homes and helped to drive you out, that ye make friends of them. Whosoever maketh friends of them - (All) such are wrong-doers

64:14.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ مِنۡ أَزۡوَٰجِكُمۡ وَأَوۡلَٰدِكُمۡ عَدُوࣰّ ا لَّكُمۡ فَٱحۡذَرُوهُمۡۚ وَإِن تَعۡفُواْ وَتَصۡفَحُواْ وَتَغۡفِرُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
64:14.en: O ye who believe! Lo! among your wives and your children there are enemies for you, therefor beware of them. And if ye efface and overlook and forgive, then lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

64:15.ar: إِنَّمَآ أَمۡوَٰلُكُمۡ وَأَوۡلَٰدُكُمۡ فِتۡنَةࣱۚ وَٱللَّهُ عِندَهُۥٓ أَجۡرٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
64:15.en: Your wealth and your children are only a temptation, whereas Allah! with Him is an immense reward

64:16.ar: فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ وَٱسۡمَعُواْ وَأَطِيعُواْ وَأَنفِقُواْ خَيۡرࣰ ا لِّأَنفُسِكُمۡۗ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
64:16.en: So keep your duty to Allah as best ye can, and listen, and obey, and spend; that is better for your souls. And whoso is saved from his own greed, such are the successful

68:48.ar: فَٱصۡبِرۡ لِحُكۡمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلۡحُوتِ إِذۡ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكۡظُومࣱ‏
68:48.en: But wait thou for thy Lord's decree, and be not like him of the fish, who cried out in despair

68:49.ar: لَّوۡلَآ أَن تَدَٰرَكَهُۥ نِعۡمَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ لَنُبِذَ بِٱلۡعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ مَذۡمُومࣱ‏
68:49.en: Had it not been that favour from his Lord had reached him he surely had been cast into the wilderness while he was reprobate

68:50.en: But his Lord chose him and placed him among the righteous

4:66.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّا كَتَبۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَنِ ٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ أَوِ ٱخۡرُجُواْ مِن دِيَٰرِكُم مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ فَعَلُواْ مَا يُوعَظُونَ بِهِۦ لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ وَأَشَدَّ تَثۡبِيتࣰ ا
4:66.en: And if We had decreed for them: Lay down your lives or go forth from your dwellings, but few of them would have done it; though if they did what they are exhorted to do it would be better for them, and more strengthening

47:36.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لَعِبࣱ وَلَهۡوࣱۚ وَإِن تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ يُؤۡتِكُمۡ أُجُورَكُمۡ وَلَا يَسۡـَٔلۡكُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلَكُمۡ
47:36.en: The life of the world is but a sport and a pastime. And if ye believe and ward off (evil). He will give you your wages, and will not ask of you your wordly wealth

47:37.ar: إِن يَسۡـَٔلۡكُمُوهَا فَيُحۡفِكُمۡ تَبۡخَلُواْ وَيُخۡرِجۡ أَضۡغَٰنَكُمۡ
47:37.en: If He should ask it of you and importune you, ye would hoard it, and He would bring to light your (secret) hates

2S00PsJ--U8.speaker: adnan
2S00PsJ--U8.speaker_note: his Ramadan night series at his centre; mentions his family roots in Nazareth and his son
2S00PsJ--U8.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 27 - Quranic Themes: Commands
2S00PsJ--U8.one_line: How to receive Quranic commands, explained through three: not allying with oppressors (60:1), caution with hostile family (64:14), and patience like Yunus lacked (68:48).
2S00PsJ--U8.summary: He opens with how a Muslim should hear the Quran's commands. A command is obligatory unless other evidence softens it, the call 'O you who believe' should make you stop and listen, and on Judgement Day the questions will mostly be about obedience to commands. Allah gains nothing from them, so every command serves us; even a harmful command would have to be obeyed, and Allah never asks for more than people could bear, such as all their wealth. The first command, 60:1, forbids taking Allah's enemies and your own as allies. It was needed because the companions leaned toward mercy, and it is needed now because leaders befriend those who openly want their people gone. Using the surah's later verses he limits it to those who fight your faith or drive you from your land, and applies it to Palestine: no alliance until everything is returned, a stance he calls basic decency rather than extremism, even if a proposed law brands it hate speech. The second, 64:14, says spouses and children can act as enemies; the answer is caution and a safe distance, never cutting family off, and pardon where possible. The third, 68:48, commands patience for Allah's decision without demanding to see the outcome, unlike Yunus who left his people too soon.

outline.heading: Opening
Commands as a major Quranic theme
outline.gist: Commands come addressed to believers, to humanity, to the Prophet and through earlier peoples; a Quranic command is obligatory unless evidence shows otherwise.

outline.heading: When a command is not an obligation
outline.gist: Only supplementary evidence in the verse, its context or the Prophet's explanation makes a command recommended, conditional or abrogated, so every command is taken seriously.

outline.heading: 'O you who believe': stop and listen
outline.gist: Commands are what we will be questioned about most: did you uphold justice, excellence, care of family as you were told?

outline.heading: Every command is in your interest
outline.gist: Allah gains nothing from obedience, so His commands protect and benefit us; even if a command were harmful it would still bind, so we have two reasons where one would do.

outline.heading: Allah never asks beyond what people can bear
outline.gist: Had He commanded self-harm, leaving homes or giving all wealth, most would refuse and their stinginess would surface; instead He asks 2.5% of idle wealth, which strengthens society.

outline.heading: 60:1: do not take My enemy and yours as allies
outline.gist: Some enemies are only personal; this verse concerns those who are enemies of both you and Allah, and he asks why such an obvious command was needed.

outline.heading: First reason: the companions' instinct to forgive
outline.gist: Islam had taught them to give the benefit of the doubt and work with everyone, so Allah had to draw a firm line for open enemies.

outline.heading: Second reason: leaders who cannot tell enemy from ally
outline.gist: The verse outlived its moment because today leaders ally with those who openly deny their people's right to exist; the verse will be held against them.

outline.heading: They expelled you for believing in Allah
outline.gist: If you migrated striving for Allah's pleasure, you cannot show love and support to those who drove out the Prophet and his followers.

outline.heading: 60:8-9: the limits of the prohibition
outline.gist: Allah allows kindness and justice toward disbelievers who did not fight your faith or expel you; only those who did, and those who aided them, are barred as allies, and one day Allah may put love between you.

outline.heading: Until the oppression stops
outline.gist: Until they stop persecuting belief and return what they took, no alliance or affection; Allah knows the love the companions hid in their hearts.

outline.heading: Palestine: no alliance until every millimetre returns
outline.gist: Not a political strategy but obedience: whatever it costs him, he will keep standing up and raise children who do the same until the land is returned and the oppression ends.

outline.heading: This is basic decency, not extremism
outline.gist: Refusing to befriend someone still oppressing you is normal human reasoning; as a child he wondered why the verse was needed, as an adult he saw people trusting those who openly plan to harm them.

outline.heading: When quoting the verse becomes hate speech
outline.gist: A proposed law could make this verse unquotable even for a descendant of Nazareth; a world run by whoever has the bigger bomb has no principles, but a Muslim stands by truth, wisely, whatever the cost.

outline.heading: Interlude
64:14: enemies among your spouses and children
outline.gist: This enmity is about competing interests, not politics; the response is not war but caution so they cannot take from you what you have built with Allah.

outline.heading: Keep a safe distance, never cut family off
outline.gist: You cannot ostracise or abandon family; no scenario of cutting off blood ends well, so keep caring and guiding while denying them the access to ruin you, and pardon if you can.

outline.heading: When the closest people turn against you
outline.gist: A Syrian proverb about spitting upward or downward and an old Arab poem of a man whose tribe killed his brother capture the bind: retaliation wounds yourself and forgiveness feels impossible.

outline.heading: Seek pardon tonight by pardoning family
outline.gist: Do not treat them as enemies even when they treat you so; on the 27th night, if you want Allah's pardon, pardon those of your blood.

outline.heading: 64:15-16: wealth and children are a test
outline.gist: Fear Allah as much as you can, listen and obey, and know that those saved from the greed of their own selves are the successful.

outline.heading: Interlude
Eid prayer belongs to the whole community
outline.gist: He will not hold a separate Eid in his own centre unless there is real need, because the sunnah is that Muslims pray Eid together rather than in half-empty separate gatherings.

outline.heading: 68:48: be patient for your Lord's decision
outline.gist: Al-Qalam has almost no practical command until its end, one of the first given to the Prophet: persevere until Allah decides; we do not choose when good prevails.

outline.heading: Make peace with not seeing the outcome
outline.gist: The Prophet died at sixty-three, only years before Islam reached three continents; we too will likely not see the results we work for.

outline.heading: Do not be like the companion of the whale
outline.gist: Yunus lost patience and left his people just before it mattered, then called out in distress from the whale; Allah's blessing rescued him, and the lesson is never to act in haste you will regret.

themes.note: Fears that quoting this verse will be treated as hate speech, in a world whose ethics follow raw power.

stories.who: The Prophet's death before Islam spread

contemporary: Palestine: no normalisation until every Palestinian returns to his family's home
Muslim-majority leaders allying with those who seek their people's destruction
A proposed Canadian hate-speech bill that he fears would make quoting 60:1 an offence
takeaways: Treat every Quranic command as binding and expect to be asked about your obedience to it.
Do not ally with or show love to those who oppress your faith and take your land until they stop and return it, while staying just and kind to everyone else.
When family members work against you, keep a safe distance without cutting them off, and pardon them when you can.
Persevere in doing good without needing to see the outcome in your lifetime.
Do not act in haste or abandon a task out of frustration just before it may bear fruit.

3:35.ar: إِذۡ قَالَتِ ٱمۡرَأَتُ عِمۡرَٰنَ رَبِّ إِنِّي نَذَرۡتُ لَكَ مَا فِي بَطۡنِي مُحَرَّرࣰ ا فَتَقَبَّلۡ مِنِّيٓۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
3:35.en: (Remember) when the wife of 'Imran said: My Lord! I have vowed unto Thee that which is in my belly as a consecrated (offering). Accept it from me. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Hearer, the Knower

3:36.ar: فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتۡهَا قَالَتۡ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَضَعۡتُهَآ أُنثَىٰ وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتۡ وَلَيۡسَ ٱلذَّكَرُ كَٱلۡأُنثَىٰۖ وَإِنِّي سَمَّيۡتُهَا مَرۡيَمَ وَإِنِّيٓ أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ
3:36.en: And when she was delivered she said: My Lord! Lo! I am delivered of a female - Allah knew best of what she was delivered - the male is not as the female; and lo! I have named her Mary, and lo! I crave Thy protection for her and for her offspring from Satan the outcast

TFLNjnX55uI.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 26: Sixth Night of Tahajjud
TFLNjnX55uI.one_line: The second half of the prayer: prostration as the closest point to Allah, a conversation rather than a list of demands, and endless reasons to seek forgiveness.
TFLNjnX55uI.summary: Continuing his nightly walk through the movements of the prayer, Sh. Adnan reaches its second half. Having stood, bowed and risen in praise, the worshipper is now allowed to move to three movements: two prostrations and the sitting between them. The Prophet told us to make much dua in prostration because it is likely to be answered, and that a servant is closest to his Lord while prostrating. Prostration is the most humble a person will ever be, a posture people never give to anyone but Allah. He asks people to treat it as a conversation with Allah, a response to the conversation Allah began through the Quran, not a list of demands with deadlines, and to learn the language of that conversation from the Prophet's duas and from the mother of Maryam speaking to her Lord at her daughter's birth. In the second reminder he explains that two prostrations give two chances to ask, and the sitting between them is for forgiveness of what has passed. The Prophet sought forgiveness a hundred times a day because his sensitivity was so high that any shortfall in his closeness to Allah warranted it, and we should seek forgiveness for not being our best, not only for sins.

outline.heading: Opening
Interlude
From the first half of the prayer to the second
outline.gist: After standing, bowing and rising to praise Allah as He deserves, the worshipper is permitted to move on to the second half: three movements.

outline.heading: Make much dua in prostration
outline.gist: The Prophet told us to make abundant dua in prostration because it is most likely to be answered.

outline.heading: Prostration: the most humble posture and the closest point
outline.gist: A servant is closest to his Lord in prostration; people once stood humbly before kings, but prostration is a humility almost no one gives to anyone besides Allah.

outline.heading: A conversation, not a list of demands
outline.gist: Treat prostration as a conversation with Allah, a response to the conversation He began through the Quran, not a list of requests you expect granted within a set time.

outline.heading: Learning to speak to Allah from the mother of Maryam
outline.gist: The Prophet's recorded duas show the words and humble attitude to use, and the Quran gives the mother of Maryam dedicating her child and naming her at birth as a model.

outline.heading: Interlude
Two prostrations, two chances to ask
outline.gist: Allah gives two prostrations so that anything you forgot to ask the first time you can ask the second time.

outline.heading: The sitting between prostrations: forgiveness for the past
outline.gist: The sitting is for asking forgiveness for what has already happened, so the three movements cover all of your time; the Prophet sought forgiveness a hundred times a day.

outline.heading: Why the Prophet sought forgiveness so often
outline.gist: If you cannot think of sins it is a matter of sensitivity; the Prophet's bar was so high that the slightest shortfall in his relationship with Allah was worth seeking forgiveness for.

outline.heading: Seek forgiveness for not being your best
outline.gist: Ask forgiveness for not being as close and focused as you could be, and invest in the praise of the first half so the requests of the second half are better.

outline.heading: Interlude
Outro
